Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 1–7:

Volume three of Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman fi Tafsir al-Qur'an, by its compiler, the poor one in need of God, Abd al-Rahman ibn Nasir ibn Sa'di, may God forgive him, his parents, and all Muslims. May God's blessings be upon our Prophet Muhammad, his family and all his companions, and may He grant them abundant peace until the Day of Judgment.

Meccan.

{1–2} God says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), showing him the greatness of the Qur'an: {A Book revealed to you}; that is, a noble Book that contains everything that servants need, all divine objectives and legislative aims, in a firm and detailed form. So let there be no {constriction} in your breast because of it; that is, no narrowness, doubt or uncertainty. Rather, know that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, to which falsehood cannot come from before it or from behind it. Let your breast be expanded by it, let your soul be at rest with it, and proclaim its commands and prohibitions, and do not fear any blamer or opponent. {So that you may warn with it}: the creation, admonish them and remind them, so that the proof is established against the obstinate, {and} let it be {a reminder for the believers}; as He said, {And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers} (51:55): they remember through it the straight path, its outward and inward deeds, and what stands between the servant and his following it.

{3} Then God addressed the servants and drew their attention to the Book, saying: {Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord}; that is, the Book which He willed to send down for your sake, and which comes {from your Lord}, who wishes to complete His nurture of you. So He sent down to you this Book, which, if you follow it, your upbringing will be perfected, His blessing will be completed upon you, and you will be guided to the best of deeds, morals and their noblest forms. {And do not follow other than Him as protectors}; that is, do not take them as allies, follow their desires, and abandon the truth for their sake. {Little do you remember}: had you remembered and recognised the benefit, you would not have preferred the harmful over the beneficial, or the enemy over the friend.

{4} Then He warned them of His punishment upon the nations who denied what their messengers brought them, so that they would not resemble them, saying: {How many a town have We destroyed, and Our might came upon it by night or while they were taking a midday rest}; that is, Our severe punishment came upon them at a time of their heedlessness and while they were unaware. Destruction had not occurred to their hearts. When the punishment came to them, they could not repel it from themselves, their gods upon whom they had relied did not avail them, and they did not disown the injustice and sins they had been committing.

{5} {So their only plea, when Our might came upon them, was to say: Indeed we were wrongdoers} (7:5); as He said: {And how many a town that was wrongdoing have We shattered, and produced after it another people. And when they perceived Our might, they fled from it. Do not flee, and return to what you were made to enjoy and your dwellings that you may be questioned. They said: Woe to us, indeed we were wrongdoers. And that remained their cry until We made them as cut-down stalks, extinguished} (21:11–15).

{6} His saying: {So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent} (7:6); that is, We will surely question the nations to whom God sent the messengers about what they answered their messengers with, {and the Day He calls them and says: What did you answer the messengers?} (28:65), and {We will surely question the messengers} about their conveying the messages of their Lord and what their nations answered them with.

{7} {So We will surely relate to them} (7:7); that is, to all creation, what they did, {with knowledge}: from Him, the Exalted, of their deeds, {and We were never absent}: at any time; as He said: {Allah has enumerated it while they forgot it} (58:6), and He said: {And We have certainly created above you seven heavens, and We were not, concerning creation, unaware} (23:17).

Then he mentioned the recompense for deeds, saying:

{8} That is: the weighing on the Day of Resurrection will be with justice and equity, in which there is no injustice or wrong in any way. ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾: meaning his good deeds outweigh his evil deeds in the balance, ﴿those are the successful ones﴾; that is, the ones who are saved from what is disliked, who attain what is loved, and to whom the great gain and everlasting happiness have come.

{9} ﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾: meaning his evil deeds outweigh, and the judgment goes to them, ﴿those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾: for the everlasting bliss has escaped them and painful punishment has befallen them, ﴿for they used to wrong Our signs﴾: in that they did not submit to them as they were obligated to do.

Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 10:

{10} He, may He be exalted, says, reminding His servants of the favour of their dwelling and their livelihood: {And We have certainly established you upon the earth}; that is, We have prepared it for you, such that you are able to build upon it, cultivate it, and benefit from it in its various ways. {And We have made for you therein means of livelihood}: from what grows out of the trees and plants, the minerals of the earth, and the various kinds of crafts and trades; for it is He who prepared it and subjected its causes to you. {Little is it that you are grateful}: to Allah, who has bestowed upon you all kinds of blessings and turned away from you all kinds of afflictions.

{11} God, addressing the children of Adam, says: ﴿And We created you﴾, by creating your origin and material from which you came forth, your father Adam (peace be upon him); ﴿then We fashioned you﴾ in the best form and the best proportion, and God taught him (Adam) that by which his inner form is completed: the names of every thing. Then He commanded the noble angels to prostrate to Adam, in honor, reverence, and in demonstration of his superiority, and they obeyed the command of their Lord. ﴿So they prostrated, all of them entirely, except Iblis﴾: he refused to prostrate to him, out of arrogance toward him and self-admiration.

{12} God rebuked him for that and said: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating when I created with My hands﴾, that is, I honored and preferred him with this distinction which was not given to anyone else, ﴿so you disobeyed My command and disregarded Me﴾. ﴿He said﴾, Iblis, contradicting his Lord: ﴿I am better than him﴾. Then he substantiated this false claim with his saying to Him: ﴿You created me from fire and You created him from clay﴾. The implication of this is that what is created from fire is superior to what is created from clay, because fire is high above clay and rises upward.

This analogy is among the most corrupt of analogies, for it is invalid in several respects:

Among them: it stands in opposition to God's command to him to prostrate, and an analogy that opposes a text is a invalid analogy. The purpose of analogy is that a ruling on which no text has come should resemble the matters that are textually stated and follow them. But an analogy that opposes them, and whose acceptance entails the nullification of the texts, is among the most abominable analogies.

Among them: his saying ﴿I am better than him﴾, by itself, is sufficient proof of Iblis's wickedness, for he substantiated his deficiency by his self-admiration and arrogance and by speaking about God without knowledge. And what deficiency is greater than this?

Among them: he lied in preferring the substance of fire over the substance of clay and dust. For the substance of clay contains humility, tranquility, and gravity, and from it appear the blessings of the earth, such as trees and varieties of plants of their different kinds and types. As for fire, it contains lightness, frivolity, and burning.

{13} For this reason, when what happened from Iblis happened, he fell from his high station to the lowest of the low. God said to him: ﴿Get down from it﴾, that is, from Paradise, ﴿it is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, because it is the abode of the good and the pure, and it is not fitting for the most wicked and evil of God's creation. ﴿So get out, for you are among the debased﴾, that is, the humiliated and abased, as a recompense for his pride and self-admiration, with humiliation and abasement.

{14–15} When the enemy of God declared his enmity toward God and toward Adam and his offspring, he asked God for respite and delay until the Day of Resurrection, so that he might have the opportunity to mislead whomever of the children of Adam he was able to. Since God's wisdom required the testing and examining of His servants, to distinguish the truthful from the liar, and who obeys Him from who obeys His enemy, He answered his request, saying: ﴿Indeed, you are among those given respite﴾.

{16} That is: Iblis said, when he was despaired and gave up hope of Allah's mercy: ﴿Because You have led me astray, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾; that is, for the creatures, ﴿Your straight path﴾; that is, I will surely keep to the path, and strive with my utmost effort to turn people away from it and to prevent them from following it.

{17} ﴿Then I will come to them from before them and behind them and from their right and from their left﴾; that is, from all directions and sides, and from every route by which he is able to achieve some of his aim concerning them. When the wicked one knew that they were weak, and that heedlessness had overcome many of them, and he was resolved to exert his utmost effort in leading them astray, he assumed, and his assumption was true, and so he said: ﴿And You will not find most of them grateful﴾. For establishing gratitude is part of following the straight path, and he wants to turn them away from it and to prevent them from fulfilling it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He only invites his party that they may become among the companions of the Blaze﴾. Allah has only alerted us to what he said and what he resolved to do so that we may take our precaution against him, prepare ourselves for our enemy, and guard ourselves against him by knowing the routes from which he comes and the entrances through which he penetrates. For this, the Exalted has bestowed upon us the most complete blessing.

{18} That is: God said to Iblis, when he said what he said: {Get out of it, disgraced and expelled}. It is an exit of humiliation and contempt, not an exit of honour. Rather, {mad'um} (disgraced), that is, blamed, {mad'hur} (expelled): removed far from God, from His mercy, and from every good. {I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together}. This is an oath from God, Exalted, that the Fire is the abode of the disobedient, and that it will certainly be filled with Iblis and his followers from among the jinn and mankind.

Then he warned Adam of his evil and his temptation, and said:

{19} That is: God Most High commanded Adam and his wife Hawwa' (Eve), whom God had bestowed upon him so that he might find rest in her, that they should eat from the Garden wherever they wished and enjoy therein whatever they desired. However, He designated for them one tree and forbade them from eating from it. God knows best what it is, and there is no benefit for us in specifying it. He made eating from it unlawful for them, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿and thus you would be among the wrongdoers﴾.

{20} They remained obedient to God's command until their enemy, Iblis (Satan), infiltrated them with his deception. He whispered to them a whisper by which he deceived them, and he disguised (the matter) to them and said: ﴿Your Lord has forbidden you from this tree only lest you become angels﴾; that is, of the kind of the angels, ﴿or lest you become among the immortals﴾, as He said in the other verse: ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾

{21} Along with this statement, he swore to them by God: ﴿Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers﴾; that is, one of the sincere advisers, since I have told you what I have told you.

{22} So they were deceived by that, and desire overcame reason in that state. ﴿And he brought them down﴾; that is, he lowered them from their lofty rank, which is distance from sins and disobedience, into being soiled by their filth, so they proceeded to eat from it. ﴿So when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them﴾; that is, the nakedness of each of them became visible after it had been concealed. The inner nakedness from piety in that state had an effect on the outer garment, so that it was stripped off, and their nakedness appeared. When their nakedness appeared, they were ashamed and began to fasten over their nakedness leaves from the trees of the Garden so that they might cover themselves thereby. ﴿And their Lord called out to them﴾: while they were in that state, rebuking and reproaching: ﴿Did I not forbid you from that tree and tell you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?﴾: Why then did you commit what was forbidden and obey your enemy?!

{23} Then God bestowed His favor upon them by accepting their repentance. They acknowledged the sin and asked God for His forgiveness, saying: ﴿Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers﴾; that is: we have committed the sin You warned us against and harmed ourselves by committing it, and we have done what causes loss if You do not forgive us by erasing the effect and punishment of the sin, and have mercy upon us by accepting repentance and granting well-being from such transgressions. So God forgave them for that. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred.﴾ ﴿Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him.﴾ This is while Iblis persists in his rebellion, not ceasing from his disobedience. Thus whoever resembles Adam in acknowledgment, asking for forgiveness, regret, and abandoning sin when sins proceed from him, his Lord chooses him and guides him; and whoever resembles Iblis when sin proceeds from him continues to increase in sins, for he does not increase in nearness to God, but only in distance.

{21} Along with this statement, he swore to them by God: ﴿Indeed, I am to you of the sincere advisers﴾; that is, one of the sincere advisers, since I have told you what I have told you.

{22} So they were deceived by that, and desire overcame reason in that state. ﴿And he brought them down﴾; that is, he lowered them from their lofty rank, which is distance from sins and disobedience, into being soiled by their filth, so they proceeded to eat from it. ﴿So when they tasted the tree, their private parts became apparent to them﴾; that is, the nakedness of each of them became visible after it had been concealed. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 27:

{27} The Exalted says, warning the children of Adam against being treated by Satan as he treated their father: {O children of Adam, let not Satan seduce you} ﴿O children of Adam, let not Satan tempt you﴾, by making disobedience appealing to you, calling you to it, and making you desire it so that you submit to him, {as he removed your parents from the Garden} ﴿as he removed your parents from the Garden﴾, and brought them down from a lofty station to a lower one. So he wants to do the same to you, and spares no effort against you until he seduces you, if he is able. Therefore, you must keep caution of him in mind, put on the armor of war between yourselves and him, and not be heedless of the places through which he can enter upon you. For he watches over you constantly, and {he sees you, he and his tribe} ﴿he sees you, he and his tribe﴾ of the jinn {from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe} ﴿from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies of those who do not believe﴾. So the absence of faith is what necessitates the bond of alliance between the human and the devil. {Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him} ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord. His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 28–30:

{28} Almighty God says, explaining the ugliness of the state of the polytheists who commit sins and attribute to God that He commanded them to do so: {And when they commit an abomination}: that is, everything that is considered shameful and reprehensible, and among it is their circumambulation of the House naked. {They say: "We found our fathers doing it"}: and they spoke truthfully in this. {"And God commanded us to do it"}: and they lied in this. For this reason God refuted this attribution, saying: {Say: "Indeed, God does not command immorality."} That is: it is not befitting to His perfection and wisdom that He should command His servants to engage in abominations, neither this which the polytheists do nor anything else. {Do you say about God what you do not know?} And what greater fabrication is there than this?

{29} Then He mentioned what He commands, saying: {Say: "My Lord has commanded justice."} That is: justice in acts of worship and in dealings, not injustice and oppression. {And set your faces [toward worship] at every mosque}: that is, turn toward God, and strive to perfect the acts of worship, especially the prayer; establish it outwardly and inwardly, and purify it of every diminishing and corrupting thing. {And call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion}: that is, intending by that His face alone, with no partner. Supplication (du'a') includes both the supplication of request (du'a' al-mas'alah) and the supplication of worship (du'a' al-'ibadah); that is, you should not desire or intend in your supplication any aim other than the servitude to God and His good pleasure. {As He originated you [so you will return]}: at first {you will return}: for resurrection. So the One who is capable of originating your creation is capable of returning it; indeed, the return is easier than the origination.

{30} {A group}: of you, {He has guided}: God; that is, He enabled them to be guided, facilitated for them its means, and turned away from them its obstacles. {And a group has been justly deserving of error}: that is, error became binding upon them due to what they caused for themselves and the means of misguidance they engaged in. Indeed, {they have taken the devils as allies instead of God}; and whoever takes the devil as an ally instead of God has certainly suffered a clear loss. So when they stripped themselves of the guardianship of the Most Merciful and preferred the guardianship of the devil, they obtained their abundant share of abandonment, were left to themselves, and suffered the greatest of losses. {And they think that they are guided}: because realities were inverted for them, so they considered falsehood to be truth and truth to be falsehood.

In these verses is evidence that the commands and prohibitions follow wisdom and benefit, for He, exalted is He, mentioned that it is inconceivable that He would command what sound minds find abominable and reject, and that He commands only justice and sincerity.

In it is also evidence that guidance is by God's grace and bounty, and that misguidance is by His forsaking the servant, when the servant, by his ignorance and wrongdoing, takes the devil as a guardian and causes misguidance for himself. And whoever thinks he is guided while he is astray has no excuse, because he is able to attain guidance; his thinking so comes only from his wrongdoing in abandoning the path that leads to guidance.

{31} After He had sent down to the children of Adam clothing to cover their private parts, and plumage, He, exalted is He, says: {O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prostration}; that is, cover your nakedness at every prayer, both obligatory and voluntary. Covering it is an adornment for the body, just as uncovering it leaves the body ugly and disfigured. It is also possible that what is meant by "adornment" here is more than that, namely clean and fine clothing. In this is a command to cover the 'awrah (nakedness) in prayer, to beautify oneself therein, and to keep the covering clean of filth and impurities. Then He said: {And eat and drink}; that is, of what Allah has provided you of good things, {but do not be excessive}: in that. Excess (israf) may consist of exceeding the sufficient measure and greed in foods that harm the body, or of increasing luxury and fastidiousness in food, drink and clothing, or of going beyond the lawful to the unlawful. {Indeed, He does not love the excessive}: for Allah hates excess, and it harms a person's body and livelihood, to the point that it may lead his condition to his being unable to meet the expenses that are obligatory upon him. In this noble verse is a command to partake of eating and drinking, and a prohibition against abandoning them and against excess in them.

{32} He, exalted is He, says, rebuking those who are obstinate and forbid what Allah has made lawful of the good things: {Say: Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has brought forth for His servants?}, meaning: the various kinds of clothing in their different varieties, and the good provisions of food and drink in all their kinds. That is: who is it who undertakes to forbid what Allah has bestowed upon His servants? And who is it who restricts for them what Allah has made ample? This widening by Allah for His servants with good things He has made so that they may be strengthened by them in His worship, so He has not permitted them except to His believing servants. Therefore He said: {Say: They are for those who believe in the life of this world, purely (for them) on the Day of Resurrection}, meaning: there is no accountability upon them for them. The implication of the verse is that whoever does not believe in Allah, but instead uses these things to aid his disobedience, then they are neither purely for him nor permissible, rather he will be punished for them and for enjoying them, and he will be questioned about the bounties on the Day of Resurrection. {Thus do We detail the verses}, meaning: We make them clear and explain them, {for a people who know}: because they are the ones who benefit from what Allah has detailed of the verses, and who know that they are from Allah, so they comprehend them and understand them.

{33} Then he mentioned the prohibited things which Allah has forbidden in every one of the laws, so He said: {Say: My Lord has only forbidden the abominations}, meaning: the great sins which are regarded as shameful and are reprehended for their ugliness and foulness, such as fornication, sodomy and the like. And His saying: {what is apparent of them and what is concealed}, meaning: the abominations related to the movements of the body and those related to the movements of the hearts, such as arrogance, self-admiration, showing off, hypocrisy and the like. {And sin and oppression without right}, meaning: the sins which make one sinful and make punishment obligatory in regard to the rights of Allah, and oppression against people in their blood, their wealth and their honour. Thus included in this are the sins related to the right of Allah and those related to the right of the servants. {And that you associate with Allah that for which He has sent down no authority}, meaning: no proof; rather, He has sent down the proof and evidence for monotheism. Shirk (associating partners with Allah) is that a creature be associated with Allah in His worship, and it may enter into this the lesser shirk, such as showing off, swearing by other than Allah and the like. {And that you say about Allah what you do not know}: concerning His names, His attributes, His actions and His law. All of these Allah has forbidden, and He has prohibited His servants from engaging in them, because of the specific and general corruptions in them, and because of the injustice and audacity against Allah, the domination over the servants of Allah, and the altering of the religion and law of Allah.

Such people, even if they enjoy the world and receive their portion of what was written for them in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), that will not avail them anything. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 40–41:

{40} He, exalted is He, informs about the punishment of those who denied His signs and did not believe in them, even though they are clear signs, and who were arrogant towards them and did not submit to their rulings but rather denied them and turned away. They are in despair of every good. Therefore the gates of heaven will not be opened for their souls when they die, and when they ascend, seeking to rise to God, they will ask permission but it will not be granted to them. Just as they did not ascend in the world to faith in God, His recognition and His love, so they will not ascend after death, for the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

The implication of the verse is that the souls of the believers, who submit to God's command and affirm His signs, will have the gates of heaven opened for them so that they ascend to God and reach where God wills of the higher world, and rejoice in nearness to their Lord and in attaining His good pleasure. As for His statement about the people of the Fire: {And they will not enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle}: the camel is the well-known beast, {through the eye of the needle}; i.e., until the camel, which is among the largest of animals in body, enters through the opening of the needle, which is among the narrowest of things. This is from the category of suspending a thing on something impossible; i.e., just as it is impossible for the camel to enter the eye of the needle, so it is impossible for those who deny God's signs to enter Paradise. God, the Exalted, said: {Indeed, whoever associates others with God, God has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire}; and He said here: {Thus do We recompense the criminals}; i.e., those whose criminality is great and whose transgression is severe.

{41} {For them from Hell is a bed}; i.e., a bedding beneath them, {and above them are coverings}; i.e., canopies of punishment enveloping them, {Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers}: those who wrong themselves, a fitting recompense. And your Lord does not wrong the servants.

{42} When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the punishment of the sinners who did wrong, He mentioned the reward of the obedient, saying: {Those who believe}: with their hearts, {and do righteous deeds}: with their limbs. Thus they combined faith and action, combined outward deeds and inward deeds, combined performing the obligations and abstaining from the prohibited things. Since His saying {and do righteous deeds} is a general expression that includes all righteous deeds, obligatory and recommended, and some of them may be beyond the servant's capacity, Allah, exalted is He, said: {We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity}; that is, to the extent that its ability can bear and that is not difficult for its power. In this case, it must fear Allah according to its capacity, and if it is unable to perform some of the obligations that others are able to perform, they are waived for it, as Allah, exalted is He, said: {Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity} [2:286], {Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it} [65:7], {He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty} [22:78], {So fear Allah as much as you are able} [64:16]. So there is no obligation with incapacity, and no prohibition under necessity. {Those}; that is, those characterized by faith and righteous action, {are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally}; that is, they will not desire to leave it, nor seek any substitute for it, because they see in it kinds of pleasures and categories of desirable things at which all aims come to a halt, and beyond which nothing higher is sought.

{43} {And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts}: This is from His generosity and kindness toward the people of Paradise, that the resentment that existed in their hearts and the rivalry among them, Allah uproots and removes, so that they become brothers, loving one another and close friends, sincerely affectionate. Allah, exalted is He, said: {And We will remove whatever resentment is in their breasts; [they will be] brothers, on couches facing one another} [15:47]. Allah creates for them of honor that by which each one of them attains joy and delight, and sees that there is no bliss above what he is in; thereby they are safe from envy and hatred, because their causes have been eliminated. [And] His saying: {Rivers will flow beneath them}; that is, they will cause them to gush forth wherever they wish and wherever they desire, whether within their palaces, in those lofty chambers, or in the gardens of Paradise beneath those flourishing orchards: rivers flowing without a trench, and bounties without any limit. {And} because they saw what Allah had bestowed upon them and honored them with, {they will say: "Praise be to Allah, who has guided us to this"}: by bestowing favor upon us, inspiring our hearts so that they believed in Him and submitted to the deeds that lead to this abode, and Allah preserved for us our faith and our deeds until He brought us by them to this abode. How excellent is the Generous Lord who initiated bounties for us and bestowed outward and inward blessings that no counter can count nor any reckoner enumerate. {And we would not have been guided if Allah had not guided us}; that is, we had no inherent capacity for guidance, had Allah not, exalted is He, bestowed favor through His guidance and through following His messengers. {Certainly the messengers of our Lord came with the truth}; that is, when they were enjoying the bliss that the messengers had informed them of, and what had been knowledge of certainty for them became the truth of certainty, they said: "We have verified and seen what the messengers promised us, and that all that they brought is the truth of certainty, with no doubt or ambiguity in it." {And they will be called}: as congratulation, honor, greeting, and respect: {"This is Paradise, which you have inherited"}; that is, you were its heirs, and it became an allotment for you, since the allotment of the disbelievers is the Fire. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 44–45:

{44 – 45} After He had mentioned the settling of each of the two groups in the two abodes, and they found what the messengers had reported and what the books had spoken of regarding reward and punishment, He, exalted is He, says: The people of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, saying: ﴿Indeed, we have found what our Lord promised us to be true﴾, when He promised us Paradise for faith and righteous deeds, so we entered it, and He showed us what He had described to us. ﴿Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true?﴾, concerning disbelief and sins. ﴿They will say, "Yes."﴾ We have found it to be true. Thus it became clear to all creatures with a clarity beyond any doubt that the promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful in statement than Allah? The doubts and confusions left them, the matter became certainty of certainties, the believers rejoiced in Allah's promise and were delighted, and the disbelievers despaired of any good and acknowledged against themselves that they deserved the punishment. ﴿Then a caller will call out between them﴾; that is, between the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise, saying: ﴿"The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"﴾; that is, His distance and removal from every good, since Allah had opened for them the doors of His mercy, but they turned themselves away from it by wrongdoing, and they barred themselves from the way of Allah and barred others, so they went astray and led others astray. Allah, exalted is He, wills that the path be straight and that the course of those traveling to Him be balanced, while these people desire it to be ﴿crooked﴾, deviating and turning away from the even way. ﴿And they are, concerning the Hereafter, disbelievers﴾: and this, which caused them to deviate from the path and to pursue the forbidden desires of the self, was their not believing in the resurrection and their not fearing punishment nor hoping for reward.

And what is understood from this [call] is that the mercy of Allah is upon the believers, His kindness encompasses them, and His bounty is continuously bestowed upon them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 46–49:

{46} That is: between the People of Paradise and the People of the Fire there is a barrier called al-A'raf (the Heights), neither part of Paradise nor part of the Fire, overlooking both abodes, and whoever is upon it observes the condition of both groups. Upon this barrier are men who recognize each of the People of Paradise and the People of the Fire by their *sima* (marks), i.e., the signs by which they are known and distinguished. So when they look at the People of Paradise, they call out to them: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾; that is, they greet them and give them salutations, and they have not yet entered Paradise, but they hope to enter it, and Allah has placed this hope in their hearts only because of the honor He intends for them.

{47} ﴿And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire﴾: and they see a dreadful scene and a terrible horror, ﴿they say: Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people﴾. So when the People of the A'raf see the People of Paradise, they hope to be with them in Paradise, and they greet them and salute them; and when their eyes turn, without their choice, toward the People of the Fire, they seek refuge [in Allah] from this condition, in general terms.

{48} Then He mentioned the specific after the general, saying: ﴿And the companions of the A'raf call out to men whom they recognize by their marks﴾: and they are from the People of the Fire, who in the world had prestige, nobility, wealth and children. The companions of the A'raf say to them, when they see them isolated in punishment, with no helper or rescuer: ﴿What did your gathering avail you?﴾: in the world, which you used to ward off hardships and to reach your aims in the world. Today it has vanished, and it benefits you nothing. Likewise, what benefit was your arrogance toward the truth, toward what it brought, and toward those who followed it?

{49} Then they pointed them out to certain people of Paradise who in the world were poor and weak, whom the People of the Fire used to mock. They said to the People of the Fire: ﴿Are these the ones﴾: whom Allah has admitted into Paradise, ﴿of whom you swore that Allah would not grant them mercy﴾: out of contempt for them, disdain, and self-admiration. You have broken your oaths, and there has appeared to you from Allah what you had not reckoned. ﴿Enter Paradise﴾: by what you used to do; that is, it was said to these weak ones, as an honor and a mark of esteem: enter Paradise by your righteous deeds. ﴿No fear shall be upon you﴾: regarding what lies ahead of hardships, ﴿nor shall you grieve﴾: over what has passed, but rather you are secure, tranquil, and joyful in every good. This is like His Exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks...﴾ until He said: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, looking on.﴾

The scholars and exegetes differed about who the People of the A'raf are and what their deeds were, and the correct view among these is that they are a people whose good deeds and bad deeds were equal: so their bad deeds did not outweigh, and they did not enter the Fire, and their good deeds did not outweigh, and they did not enter Paradise. They remain on the A'raf for as long as Allah wills; then Allah, the Exalted, will admit them into Paradise by His mercy, for His mercy precedes and overcomes His wrath, and His mercy encompasses all things.

He istawa in a manner befitting His majesty, greatness and sovereignty. He istawa upon the Throne, took possession of the dominion, managed the kingdoms, and executed upon them His universal decrees and His legislative commands. He is blessed in Himself, due to the greatness and perfection of His attributes, and He bestows blessing on others by causing abundant good and great benevolence to descend. Every blessing in the universe is thus among the effects of His mercy. For this reason He said: {Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds} (tabaraka Allah rabb al-'alamin).

Having mentioned of His greatness and majesty what indicates to people of understanding that He alone is the one worshipped and sought in all needs, He commanded what follows from that, saying:

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 55–56:

{55} The supplication (du'a') includes both supplication of asking (du'a' al-mas'alah) and supplication of worship (du'a' al-'ibadah). So He commanded His servants to call upon Him ﴿with humility and in secret﴾; that is, with insistence in asking and persistence in worship, and ﴿in secret﴾; that is, not aloud and openly, where one might fear showing off (riya'), but in secret and with sincerity to Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Indeed, He does not like the transgressors﴾; that is, those who exceed the limit in all matters. Among transgression is that the servant asks Allah for things that are not fitting for him, or is excessive (yatanta') in asking, or exaggerates in raising his voice in supplication. All of this falls within the forbidden transgression.

{56} ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth﴾: by committing sins (ma'asi) ﴿after its reformation﴾: by acts of obedience (ta'at). For sins corrupt character, deeds and provision, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾. Just as acts of obedience reform through them character, deeds, provision, and the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope﴾; that is, in fear of His punishment and in hope of His reward, hoping for its acceptance and fearing its rejection, not the supplication of a servant who is presumptuous toward his Lord, whose self has become pleased with itself and who has raised himself above his station, or the supplication of one who is heedless and distracted.

The summary of what Allah mentioned of the etiquettes of supplication: sincerity in it to Allah alone, for that is included in ﴿in secret﴾, and concealing and keeping it private; that the heart be fearful and hopeful, neither heedless, nor secure, nor indifferent to being answered. This is part of doing supplication well (ihsan al-du'a'), for ihsan in every act of worship is exerting effort in it and performing it complete, without any deficiency in any respect. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾: in worshipping Allah, those who do good to the servants of Allah. Whenever the servant is more excellent in doing good, he is nearer to the mercy of his Lord, and his Lord is near to him with His mercy. In this is an encouragement to excellence that is not hidden.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 55–56:

{55} The supplication (du'a') includes both supplication of asking (du'a' al-mas'alah) and supplication of worship (du'a' al-'ibadah). So He commanded His servants to call upon Him ﴿with humility and in secret﴾; that is, with insistence in asking and persistence in worship, and ﴿in secret﴾; that is, not aloud and openly, where one might fear showing off (riya'), but in secret and with sincerity to Allah, the Exalted. ﴿Indeed, He does not like the transgressors﴾; that is, those who exceed the limit in all matters. Among transgression is that the servant asks Allah for things that are not fitting for him, or is excessive (yatanta') in asking, or exaggerates in raising his voice in supplication. All of this falls within the forbidden transgression.

{56} ﴿And do not cause corruption on the earth﴾: by committing sins (ma'asi) ﴿after its reformation﴾: by acts of obedience (ta'at). For sins corrupt character, deeds and provision, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea by what the hands of people have earned﴾. Just as acts of obedience reform through them character, deeds, provision, and the affairs of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And call upon Him in fear and in hope﴾; that is, in fear of His punishment and in hope of His reward, hoping for its acceptance and fearing its rejection, not the supplication of a servant who is presumptuous toward his Lord, whose self has become pleased with itself and who has raised himself above his station, or the supplication of one who is heedless and distracted.

The summary of what Allah mentioned of the etiquettes of supplication: sincerity in it to Allah alone, for that is included in ﴿in secret﴾, and concealing and keeping it private; that the heart be fearful and hopeful, neither heedless, nor secure, nor indifferent to being answered. This is part of doing supplication well (ihsan al-du'a'), for ihsan in every act of worship is exerting effort in it and performing it complete, without any deficiency in any respect. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good﴾: in worshipping Allah, those who do good to the servants of Allah. Whenever the servant is more excellent in doing good, he is nearer to the mercy of his Lord, and his Lord is near to him with His mercy. In this is an encouragement to excellence that is not hidden.

{57} Almighty God mentions one of the signs of His power and a breath of His mercy, saying: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾; that is, the winds that bring glad tidings of rain, which stir up the rain from the earth by God's permission, so that people rejoice in God's mercy, and their hearts are comforted by it before it descends. ﴿Until, when they carry heavy clouds﴾: the winds carry them, one wind having raised them, another wind gathering them, and yet another wind fertilizing them. ﴿We drive them to a dead land﴾: a land whose animals were nearly destroyed and whose people were nearly despairing of God's mercy. ﴿Then We send down water with it﴾; that is, with that dead land, ﴿the water﴾: abundant water from those clouds. God subjected to it a wind that pours it out and a wind that disperses it, by God's permission. ﴿Then We bring forth with it all kinds of fruits﴾: so they become joyful in God's mercy and graze in God's bounty. His saying: ﴿Thus do We bring forth the dead﴾; that is, just as We revived the earth after its death through vegetation, so too will We bring forth the dead from their graves after they had become scattered decayed bones. This is clear proof, for there is no difference between the two matters. Whoever denies resurrection, considering it far-fetched, while seeing its like, does so out of obstinacy and denial of what is evident. In this is an exhortation to remember and reflect upon God's bounties and to look at them with the eye of contemplation and inference, not with the eye of heedlessness and neglect.

{58} Then He mentions the differences among the lands on which rain descends, saying: ﴿And the good land﴾; that is, good in soil and substance, when rain descends upon it, ﴿its vegetation comes forth﴾, which it is prepared to produce, ﴿by the permission of its Lord﴾; that is, by God's will and volition, for means are not independent in bringing things into existence unless God permits it. ﴿And that which is bad﴾ of lands ﴿comes forth only sparsely﴾; that is, produces only meager vegetation with no benefit or blessing. ﴿Thus do We vary the signs for a people who give thanks﴾; that is, We diversify them, clarify them, coin parables in them, and bring them forth for a people who thank God by acknowledging His blessings, affirming them, and employing them in what pleases God. These are the ones who benefit from what God has detailed in His Book of rulings and divine purposes, for they regard them as among the greatest blessings reaching them from their Lord, so they receive them in need of them and rejoicing in them, contemplating and reflecting upon them, and their meanings become clear to them according to their readiness.

This is an example for hearts when revelation descends upon them, which is the substance of life just as rain is the substance of life. Good hearts, when revelation comes to them, accept it, learn it, and grow according to the goodness of their origin and the excellence of their nature. As for corrupt hearts with no good in them, when revelation comes to them, it finds no receptive place; rather, it finds them heedless, averse, or opposing, so it is like rain that passes over salt flats, sand, and rocks without affecting them at all. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, so valleys flow according to their measure, and the torrent carries a swelling foam...﴾ and the verses that follow.

{59} Concerning Nuh (Noah), the first of the messengers, He says: ﴿We certainly sent Nuh to his people﴾. He called them to worship Allah alone at a time when they were worshipping idols. ﴿He said﴾ to them: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him﴾; that is, make Him one (tawhid), ﴿for He is the Creator, the Provider, the Manager of all affairs, and whatever else is other than Him is a created thing, managed, having no share in the affair at all.﴾ Then he warned them, if they did not obey Him, of the punishment of Allah, saying: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾. This is from his sincere advice and compassion for them, as he feared for them everlasting torment and endless misery, like his brothers among the messengers, who have greater compassion for creation than their fathers and mothers have.

{60} When he said this to them, they responded with the most ugly response. ﴿The eminent ones of his people﴾, that is, the leaders, the wealthy, the ones who are followed, whose custom is arrogance toward the truth and refusal to submit to the messengers, said: ﴿Indeed, we see you in clear error﴾. Allah disfigure them. It was not enough for them that they did not submit to him; rather, they became arrogant toward submitting to him, disparaged him in the gravest manner, attributed to him error, and did not stop at mere error, but made it a manifest error, clear to everyone!! This is among the greatest kinds of obstinacy, which cannot pass upon the weakest of minds. This description applies to the people of Nuh, who came to idols they had fashioned and carved with their own hands from lifeless objects that neither hear, nor see, nor avail them anything. They elevated them to the station of the Originator of the heavens, and directed to them every kind of act of devotion they could. Were it not that they had minds through which Allah's proof is established against them, they would be judged as being more guided than the insane; rather, they were more guided and more intelligent than them.

{61–62} So Nuh responded to them with a gentle reply and softness toward them, perhaps they would submit to him. He said: ﴿O my people, there is no error in me﴾; that is, I am not astray in any matter from any aspect; rather I am a guide who is guided. His guidance, peace be upon him, is of the same kind as the guidance of his brothers, the messengers of steadfast resolve, the highest, most complete and perfect kinds of guidance, the guidance of the complete and perfect message. For this reason he said: ﴿But I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds﴾; that is, my Lord and your Lord and the Lord of all creation, who has nurtured all creation with every kind of nurturing, among the greatest of whose nurturing is that He sent to His servants messengers who command them to righteous deeds, noble character, and good beliefs, and forbid them from their opposites. For this reason he said: ﴿I convey to you the messages of my Lord and I give you sincere advice﴾; that is, my duty is to convey to you the clarification of His oneness, His commands and prohibitions, in the manner of sincere advice to you and compassion for you. ﴿And I know from Allah what you do not know﴾. So what is necessary is that you obey me and submit to my command, if you have knowledge.

{63} ﴿Do you wonder that a reminder from your Lord has come to you through a man from among you?﴾; that is, how can you be astonished at a situation that should not cause astonishment: that reminder, admonition and advice has come to you through the hand of a man from among you, whose reality, truthfulness and condition you know. This situation is from Allah's care for you, His goodness and His kindness, which should be received with acceptance and gratitude. As for His saying: ﴿so that he may warn you, and that you may fear Allah, and that you may receive mercy﴾; that is, so that he may warn you of the painful punishment, and that you may take the means that save you, by practicing the fear of Allah outwardly and inwardly, and by this you will attain it, and the vast mercy of Allah will descend upon you.

{64} But it did not benefit them, nor did it succeed. ﴿So they denied him, and We saved him and those with him in the ship﴾; that is, the ship which Allah commanded Nuh, peace be upon him, to build, and revealed to him that he should carry from every kind of animal two pairs, and his family, and those who believed with him. He carried them in it, and Allah saved them by means of it. ﴿And We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people﴾, blind to guidance; they had seen the truth, but Allah had shown them through the hand of Nuh clear signs by which those of understanding believe, yet they mocked him, ridiculed him, and disbelieved.

Then he explained it by his words: ﴿This is the she-camel of God as a sign for you.﴾ That is, this is a noble, excellent she-camel, given honour by its attribution to God, and for you in it is a great sign. The aspect of the sign has been mentioned in His words: ﴿for her is a drink, and for you is a drink on a known day.﴾ They had a large well, known as the well of the she-camel, which they and the she-camel took turns to use: the she-camel had a day when she drank, and they drank the milk from her udder, and they had a day when they came to water and the she-camel departed from them. Their prophet Salih, peace be upon him, said to them: ﴿So leave her to feed on God's earth,﴾ meaning, there is no burden on you for her sustenance, ﴿and do not touch her with harm,﴾ that is, by hamstringing her or otherwise, ﴿lest a painful punishment seize you.﴾

{74} ﴿And remember when He made you successors﴾ on the earth, to enjoy it and attain your aims, ﴿after 'Ad,﴾ those whom God destroyed, and He made you their successors, ﴿and settled you in the land,﴾ that is, He established you in it and facilitated for you the means that lead to what you desire and seek, ﴿taking from its plains palaces,﴾ that is, from the flat lands that are not mountains, you took houses, and from the mountains you took houses which you carved out, as their works in the mountains, the dwellings and the Hijr and the like, which remain visible to this day, are still standing as long as the mountains remain. ﴿So remember the blessings of God﴾ — that is, His favours and what He has bestowed upon you of bounty, provision and strength — ﴿and do not go about in the land causing corruption.﴾ That is, do not ruin the land through corruption and sins; for sins leave flourishing homes as desolate wastes, and they have emptied their dwellings of them and left their houses desolate after them.

{75} ﴿The eminent ones of his people who were arrogant said to those who were oppressed﴾: that is, the leaders and nobles who were haughty towards the truth. Since the oppressed were not all believers, they said: ﴿to those among them who believed: "Do you know that Salih is sent from his Lord?"﴾ That is, is he truthful or a liar? The oppressed said: ﴿Indeed, we believe in that with which he was sent,﴾ namely the monotheism of God, and what he reported about Him, and His commands and prohibitions.

{76} ﴿Those who were arrogant said: "Indeed, we disbelieve in that which you believe."﴾ Arrogance led them not to submit to the truth to which the weak had submitted.

{77} ﴿Then they hamstrung the she-camel,﴾ which he had warned them that if they touched her with harm, a painful punishment would befall them. ﴿And they defied the command of their Lord﴾; that is, they were insolent towards it and arrogant towards His command, and whoever defies it, God makes him taste severe punishment. Without doubt, God brought upon them such retribution as He had not brought upon others. ﴿And they said﴾, with these acts, daring against God, seeking to defeat Him, unconcerned by what they had done, but rather boasting of them: ﴿O Salih, bring us what you threaten us with — if you are of the truthful — of punishment.﴾ He said: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days; that is a promise not to be denied.﴾

{78} ﴿So the earthquake seized them, and they became in their homes prostrate,﴾ on their knees; God destroyed them and cut off their last trace.

{79} ﴿So he turned away from them,﴾ Salih, peace be upon him, when God brought the punishment upon them, ﴿and said﴾, addressing them with rebuke and reproach after God had destroyed them: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you sincerely﴾; that is, I have conveyed to you everything God sent me with, I was eager for your guidance, and I strove to lead you upon the straight path and the upright religion, ﴿but you do not love sincere advisers﴾: rather, you rejected the words of the sincere counsellors and obeyed every accursed devil.

Know that many exegetes mention in this story that the she-camel came out of a hard, smooth rock which they demanded of Salih, and that it writhed like a pregnant woman in labour, and the she-camel emerged while they watched; and that when they hamstrung her she had a young camel which cried out three times and the mountain split open for it and it entered it; and that Salih, peace be upon him, told them: the sign of the descent of the punishment upon you is that on the first of the three days your faces will be yellow, on the second red, and on the third black, and so it happened as he said.

This is among the Israelite narrations which should not be transmitted in the interpretation of God's Book, and there is nothing in the Qur'an that indicates any of it in any way. Indeed, had it been sound, God would have mentioned it, since it contains wonders, lessons and signs that He would not neglect or leave unmentioned, to be transmitted through a channel whose narrator is not trusted. Rather, the Qur'an contradicts some of these reports, for Salih said to them: ﴿Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three [days]﴾; that is, take pleasure and delight in this very short time, for you have no enjoyment or delight beyond it. And what pleasure and enjoyment is there for those whose prophet promised them the descent of punishment and told them of its preliminary signs, which then befell them day by day in a manner that encompassed and included them all? Is the reddening, yellowing and blackening of their faces not from the punishment? Is this not contrary to the Qur'an and opposed to it? The Qur'an contains sufficiency and guidance apart from anything else. Yes, if anything is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, which does not contradict the Book of God, it is to be accepted with the utmost respect, and it is of what the Qur'an commanded us to follow: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it.﴾ It has already been mentioned that it is not permissible to interpret the Book of God by Israelite reports, even if narrating from them is permitted regarding matters whose falsehood is not certain; for the meanings of God's Book are certain, whereas those matters are neither to be affirmed nor denied, so the two cannot be reconciled.

(80) That is: {And} mention Our servant {Lut} (peace be upon him), when We sent him to his people, commanding them to worship Allah alone and forbidding them from the abomination which no one among the worlds had committed before them. So he said: {Do you commit an abomination that no one among the worlds has preceded you in?} That is, the deed which reached such magnitude and foulness that it encompassed all kinds of indecency. That it is an abomination, and that they invented it, originated it, and set it as a precedent for those after them, are all among the most heinous of things.

(81) Then he explained it by saying: {Indeed, you approach men lustfully instead of women.} That is: how do you forsake the women whom Allah created for you, in whom there is lawful enjoyment that accords with desire and natural disposition, and instead turn to the posteriors of men, which is the utmost in shamefulness and corruption, a place from which emerge filth and impurities that one is ashamed to mention, let alone touch or approach? {Rather, you are a people who transgress}: that is, you exceed what Allah has set as limits, and you are bold in violating His sacred prohibitions.

(82) {And the answer of his people was only that they said, "Expel them from your town; indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure."} That is, they abstain from committing the abomination. {And they did not resent them except that they believed in Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.}

(83) {So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was among those who remained behind.} That is, among those who were left to be punished. Allah commanded him to travel with his family by night, for the punishment would come upon his people at dawn. So he set out with them, except his wife, upon whom befell what befell them.

(84) {And We rained upon them a rain} That is, scorching, severe stones of sijjil, and Allah turned its upper part to its lower part. {So look at how was the end of the criminals}: destruction and everlasting disgrace.

{85} And ﴿We sent﴾ to the people known as Madyan ﴿their brother Shu'ayb﴾ by lineage. He called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and commanded them to give full measure and weight, not to defraud people of their things, and not to ﴿spread corruption in the earth﴾ by committing much sin. Therefore he said: ﴿And do not spread corruption in the earth after it has been set in order. That is better for you, if you are believers.﴾ Abandoning sins in obedience to Allah's command and seeking nearness to Him is better and more beneficial for the servant than committing them, which brings on the wrath of the Almighty and the punishment of the Fire.

{86} ﴿Do not sit on every path﴾, meaning every road that is much travelled, ﴿threatening﴾ those who walk it and ﴿turning away from the way of Allah﴾ those who wish to be guided by it, ﴿and seeking to make it crooked﴾, meaning you seek to make the way of Allah crooked and bend it to follow your desires. It was obligatory upon you and upon others to show respect and honour to the way that Allah established for His servants, so that they might travel it to His good pleasure and the abode of His honour, and He had shown them the greatest mercy by it. You should have stood to support it, to call to it and to defend it, not to become the highwaymen who block people from it. This is ingratitude for the blessing of Allah, opposition to Allah, and making the straightest and most just path crooked, and mocking those who follow it. ﴿And remember﴾ Allah's blessing upon you ﴿when you were few, and He multiplied you﴾, meaning He increased you by the blessings He bestowed: wives, offspring and health. He did not afflict you with plague or with diseases that diminish your numbers, nor did He give an enemy power over you to annihilate you, nor scatter you across the earth; rather He blessed you with unity, abundant provision and increase of offspring. ﴿And see how was the end of the corrupters﴾. You will find in their assemblies nothing but dispersal, and in their dwellings nothing but desolation and ruin. They left no good remembrance behind them; rather they were followed in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection [they will be] in greater shame and disgrace.

{87} ﴿If a group of you believe in what I have been sent with, and a group does not believe﴾, namely the majority of them, ﴿then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges﴾, that He may grant victory to the righteous and inflict punishment upon the falsifier.

{88} ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said﴾: they were the nobles and elders among them, who followed their desires and were occupied with their pleasures. When the truth came to them and they saw that it did not agree with their corrupt desires, they rejected it and were arrogant towards it. They said to their prophet Shu'ayb and to those believers who were weak with him: ﴿We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return to our religion.﴾ They used their beastly strength against the truth, and did not respect religion, covenant or any right. They only respected and followed their desires and their foolish minds, which led them to this corrupt statement. They said, in effect: either you and those with you return to our religion, or we will expel you from our town. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had been calling them in hope of their faith, but now they, in threatening him with exile from his homeland, which he and those with him had more right to than they did, did not leave him safe from their evil until they threatened him if he did not follow them. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said to them, marvelling at their words: ﴿Even though we were averse?﴾, meaning: will we follow you in your religion and your false creed even though we are averse to it? We would know its falsehood, for one only invites to it someone who has some desire for it. As for one who openly forbids it and denounces those who follow it, how could he be invited to it?

{89} ﴿We would have invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has rescued us from it.﴾ That is: bear witness against us that if we return [to it] after Allah has rescued us and delivered us from its evil, we are liars who fabricate lies against Allah. We know that there is no greater fabrication than from one who makes a partner for Allah, while He is the One, the Unique, the Eternal Refuge, who has taken no consort, nor son, nor partner in dominion. ﴿It is not for us to return to it﴾, meaning it is impossible for the likes of us to return to it, for this is inconceivable. Thus, peace be upon him, he made them despair of his agreeing with them, for several reasons:
From one aspect, they are averse to it and detest what they are upon of shirk.
From another, he declared what they were upon to be a lie, and made them witness that if he and those with him followed them, they would be liars.
Among them is their acknowledgement of Allah's favour upon them in rescuing them from it.
Among them is that returning to it after Allah has guided them is impossible, considering their present state and what is in their hearts of glorifying Allah, acknowledging His lordship, and that He alone is the God whom alone worship is due, without partner, and that the gods of the polytheists are the falsest falsehood and the most impossible of impossibilities. Since Allah has blessed them with minds by which they can recognise truth and falsehood, guidance and error.
As for viewing it in terms of Allah's will and His all-pervading decree over His creation, from which no one can escape even if causes are multiplied and powers align, they cannot judge concerning themselves that they will do something or leave it. Therefore he made an exception: ﴿Unless Allah, our Lord, wills.﴾ That is: neither we nor anyone else can escape His will, which follows from His knowledge and wisdom. ﴿Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾, so He knows what is good for the servants and how He manages them. ﴿In Allah we have put our trust﴾, meaning we rely on Him to keep us firm upon the straight path and to protect us from all the paths of Hellfire, for whoever trusts in Allah, He suffices him and makes easy for him the affairs of his religion and his worldly life. ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾, meaning grant victory to the oppressed and the one with right against the oppressor who opposes the truth. ﴿And You are the best of deciders.﴾ His opening [judgement] for His servants is of two kinds: the opening of knowledge, by making clear truth from falsehood, guidance from error, and who is upright upon the path from who has deviated from it; and the second kind is the opening through recompense, inflicting punishment upon the wrongdoers, and salvation and honour for the righteous. They asked Allah to decide between them and their people with truth and justice, and to show them from His signs and lessons what would be a decisive separation between the two parties.

{90} ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who disbelieved said﴾, warning against following Shu'ayb: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you will be losers.﴾ This is what their souls embellished for them: that loss and misery lie in following rectitude and guidance. They did not realise that complete loss lies in clinging to their own error and misguiding others, and they knew this when the punishment befell them.

{91} ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, that is, the severe quake, ﴿and they became in their homes prostrate﴾, that is, fallen dead and motionless.

{92} Allah the Exalted said, lamenting their state: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were as if they had never prospered therein.﴾ That is: as if they had never dwelt in their homes, never enjoyed themselves in their courtyards, never sheltered in their shade, never flourished among the pastures of their rivers, and never eaten from the fruits of their trees. Then the punishment seized them and moved them from the place of amusement, play and pleasures to the abode of grief, misery, punishment and the lowest depths. Therefore He said: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were the losers.﴾ That is: the loss is confined to them, for they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Surely that is the manifest loss, not [the loss of] those who said to them: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you will be losers.﴾

{91} ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, that is, the severe quake, ﴿and they became in their homes prostrate﴾, that is, fallen dead and motionless.

Therefore he made an exception: ﴿Unless Allah, our Lord, wills.﴾ That is: neither we nor anyone else can escape His will, which follows from His knowledge and wisdom. ﴿Our Lord encompasses all things in knowledge﴾, so He knows what is good for the servants and how He manages them. ﴿In Allah we have put our trust﴾, meaning we rely on Him to keep us firm upon the straight path and to protect us from all the paths of Hellfire, for whoever trusts in Allah, He suffices him and makes easy for him the affairs of his religion and his worldly life. ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth﴾, meaning grant victory to the oppressed and the one with right against the oppressor who opposes the truth. ﴿And You are the best of deciders.﴾ His opening [judgement] for His servants is of two kinds: the opening of knowledge, by making clear truth from falsehood, guidance from error, and who is upright upon the path from who has deviated from it; and the second kind is the opening through recompense, inflicting punishment upon the wrongdoers, and salvation and honour for the righteous. They asked Allah to decide between them and their people with truth and justice, and to show them from His signs and lessons what would be a decisive separation between the two parties.

{90} ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who disbelieved said﴾, warning against following Shu'ayb: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you will be losers.﴾ This is what their souls embellished for them: that loss and misery lie in following rectitude and guidance. They did not realise that complete loss lies in clinging to their own error and misguiding others, and they knew this when the punishment befell them.

{91} ﴿So the earthquake seized them﴾, that is, the severe quake, ﴿and they became in their homes prostrate﴾, that is, fallen dead and motionless.

{92} Allah the Exalted said, lamenting their state: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were as if they had never prospered therein.﴾ That is: as if they had never dwelt in their homes, never enjoyed themselves in their courtyards, never sheltered in their shade, never flourished among the pastures of their rivers, and never eaten from the fruits of their trees. Then the punishment seized them and moved them from the place of amusement, play and pleasures to the abode of grief, misery, punishment and the lowest depths. Therefore He said: ﴿Those who denied Shu'ayb were the losers.﴾ That is: the loss is confined to them, for they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Surely that is the manifest loss, not [the loss of] those who said to them: ﴿If you follow Shu'ayb, then indeed you will be losers.﴾

{93} When they perished, their prophet, peace be upon him, turned away from them and ﴿said﴾, rebuking, reproaching and addressing them after their death: ﴿O my people, I had certainly conveyed to you the messages of my Lord﴾, that is, I delivered them to you and explained them until they reached you to the utmost extent possible and penetrated your hearts. ﴿And I advised you﴾, but you did not accept my advice nor submit to my guidance; rather you transgressed and rebelled. ﴿So how could I grieve over a disbelieving people?﴾ That is: how could I grieve over a people in whom there is no good, to whom goodness came and they rejected it and did not accept it, and who deserve nothing but evil? Such people are not worthy of being grieved over; rather one should rejoice at their destruction and annihilation. So we seek refuge in You, O Allah, from disgrace and shame! And what misery and punishment could be more severe than to reach a state in which the most sincere of all creatures towards them disowns them?!

{85} And ﴿We sent﴾ to the people known as Madyan ﴿their brother Shu'ayb﴾ by lineage. He called them to worship Allah alone, without partner, and commanded them to give full measure and weight, not to defraud people of their things, and not to ﴿spread corruption in the earth﴾ by committing much sin. Therefore he said: ﴿And do not spread corruption in the earth after it has been set in order. That is better for you, if you are believers.﴾ Abandoning sins in obedience to Allah's command and seeking nearness to Him is better and more beneficial for the servant than committing them, which brings on the wrath of the Almighty and the punishment of the Fire.

{86} ﴿Do not sit on every path﴾, meaning every road that is much travelled, ﴿threatening﴾ those who walk it and ﴿turning away from the way of Allah﴾ those who wish to be guided by it, ﴿and seeking to make it crooked﴾, meaning you seek to make the way of Allah crooked and bend it to follow your desires. It was obligatory upon you and upon others to show respect and honour to the way that Allah established for His servants, so that they might travel it to His good pleasure and the abode of His honour, and He had shown them the greatest mercy by it. You should have stood to support it, to call to it and to defend it, not to become the highwaymen who block people from it. This is ingratitude for the blessing of Allah, opposition to Allah, and making the straightest and most just path crooked, and mocking those who follow it. ﴿And remember﴾ Allah's blessing upon you ﴿when you were few, and He multiplied you﴾, meaning He increased you by the blessings He bestowed: wives, offspring and health. He did not afflict you with plague or with diseases that diminish your numbers, nor did He give an enemy power over you to annihilate you, nor scatter you across the earth; rather He blessed you with unity, abundant provision and increase of offspring. ﴿And see how was the end of the corrupters﴾. You will find in their assemblies nothing but dispersal, and in their dwellings nothing but desolation and ruin. They left no good remembrance behind them; rather they were followed in this world by a curse, and on the Day of Resurrection [they will be] in greater shame and disgrace.

{87} ﴿If a group of you believe in what I have been sent with, and a group does not believe﴾, namely the majority of them, ﴿then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges﴾, that He may grant victory to the righteous and inflict punishment upon the falsifier.

{88} ﴿The chiefs of those of his people who were arrogant said﴾: they were the nobles and elders among them, who followed their desires and were occupied with their pleasures. When the truth came to them and they saw that it did not agree with their corrupt desires, they rejected it and were arrogant towards it. They said to their prophet Shu'ayb and to those believers who were weak with him: ﴿We will surely expel you, O Shu'ayb, and those who believe with you from our town, or you will return to our religion.﴾ They used their beastly strength against the truth, and did not respect religion, covenant or any right. They only respected and followed their desires and their foolish minds, which led them to this corrupt statement. They said, in effect: either you and those with you return to our religion, or we will expel you from our town. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, had been calling them in hope of their faith, but now they, in threatening him with exile from his homeland, which he and those with him had more right to than they did, did not leave him safe from their evil until they threatened him if he did not follow them. Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, said to them, marvelling at their words: ﴿Even though we were averse?﴾, meaning: will we follow you in your religion and your false creed even though we are averse to it? We would know its falsehood, for one only invites to it someone who has some desire for it. As for one who openly forbids it and denounces those who follow it, how could he be invited to it?

{89} ﴿We would have invented a lie against Allah if we returned to your religion after Allah has rescued us from it.﴾ That is: bear witness against us that if we return [to it] after Allah has rescued us and delivered us from its evil, we are liars who fabricate lies against Allah. Thus, peace be upon him, he made them despair of his agreeing with them, for several reasons:
From one aspect, they are averse to it and detest what they are upon of shirk.
From another, he declared what they were upon to be a lie, and made them witness that if he and those with him followed them, they would be liars.
Among them is their acknowledgement of Allah's favour upon them in rescuing them from it.
Among them is that returning to it after Allah has guided them is impossible, considering their present state and what is in their hearts of glorifying Allah, acknowledging His lordship, and that He alone is the God whom alone worship is due, without partner, and that the gods of the polytheists are the falsest falsehood and the most impossible of impossibilities. {95} {Then}: when this did not benefit them, their arrogance persisted and their rebellion increased, {We replaced the bad with good}: We showered upon them provisions, granted health to their bodies, and lifted the trials from them, {until they multiplied}; meaning, they grew in number, their provisions increased, and they expanded in the blessings and bounty of God, forgetting the trials that had passed over them. {And they said: "Hardship and ease touched our fathers as well"}; meaning, this is a customary pattern that has never ceased to exist among earlier and later generations: at times they are in ease, at times in hardship, at times in joy, and at times in sorrow, according to the fluctuations of time and the alternation of days. They reckoned that these were neither an admonition and reminder nor a means of gradual testing and a warning. Until, when they rejoiced and exulted in what they had been given, and the world was at its most pleasing to them, We seized them with punishment {suddenly, while they did not perceive}; meaning, destruction did not occur to their minds, and they thought they were capable of what God had given them, and that they would not cease or be removed from it.
