For this reason Allah, in this verse, made seeing Him conditional upon the firmness of the mountain, so He said, persuading Musa not to be granted his request: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place﴾, that is, when Allah manifests Himself to it, ﴿then you will see Me.﴾ ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾, the solid, massive one, ﴿He made it crumble to dust﴾, that is, it collapsed like sand, in alarm at the sight of Allah and its inability to remain steadfast. ﴿And Musa fell unconscious﴾ when he saw what he saw. Then it became clear to him that if the mountain could not remain steady before the sight of Allah, Musa was even less able to remain steady. He sought forgiveness from his Lord for what had come from him of the request that was not fitting for its place. He said: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, I declare You far exalted above and magnify You beyond what is unworthy of Your majesty. ﴿I have repented to You﴾ from all sins and from any lack of good manners toward You. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾, that is, peace and blessings be upon him, renewed his faith by what Allah perfected for him of what he had been ignorant of before that.

{144} When Allah prevented him from seeing Him after he had been longing for it, He gave him abundant good. He said: ﴿O Musa, indeed I have chosen you over the people﴾, that is, I have selected you, chosen you, preferred you, and singled you out with great virtues and noble distinctions, ﴿by My messages﴾, which I do not assign nor single out except to the most excellent of creation, ﴿and by My speech﴾ to you without intermediary. This is a virtue in which Musa was singled out, the one known among his brother messengers as al-Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah). ﴿So take what I have given you﴾ of the blessings, and take what I have given you of commands and prohibitions with an open breast, and receive it with acceptance and submission. ﴿And be among the grateful﴾ to Allah for what He has singled you out for and preferred you with.

{145} ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets concerning all things﴾ that people need, ﴿an admonition﴾ that inclines souls toward acts of goodness and deters them from acts of evil, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ of the legal rulings, beliefs, morals, and etiquettes. ﴿So take them with strength﴾, that is, with earnestness and diligence in establishing them. ﴿And enjoin your people to take the best of them﴾, which are the obligatory and recommended commands, for these are the best of them. In this there is evidence that Allah's commands in every law are complete, just, and good. ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾, after Allah destroyed them and left their dwellings as a lesson for those after them, by which the rightly guided, humble believers may take heed.

{146} As for others, He said concerning them: ﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾, that is, from taking heed of the signs of the horizons and of the self, and from understanding the verses of the Book, ﴿those who are arrogant upon the earth without right﴾, that is, who act arrogantly toward the servants of Allah, toward the truth, and toward the one who brought it. Whoever has this characteristic, Allah deprives him of abundant good and forsakes him, and he does not understand from the signs of Allah that which would benefit him. Indeed, realities may be inverted for him and he may come to regard ugliness as beautiful. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾, because of their aversion, their opposition, and their hostility toward Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance﴾, that is, guidance and uprightness, which is the path that leads to Allah and to the abode of His honour, ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾, that is, they will not follow it nor desire it. ﴿And if they see the way of error﴾, that is, the misguidance that leads its companion to the abode of misery, ﴿they will take it as a way.﴾ The cause of their deviation into this deviation is: ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾. Their rejection of the signs of Allah, their heedlessness of what they are intended to convey, and their contempt for them is what caused them to follow the path of error and abandon the path of right guidance, with what that necessitated.

{147} ﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾, the great ones indicating the truth of what We sent Our messengers with, ﴿and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾, ﴿their deeds have become worthless﴾, because they were not founded on a basis, and their condition, which is faith in the signs of Allah and belief in His recompense, was lacking. ﴿Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ That is, in the nullification of their deeds and the attainment of the opposite of their intended aims. For the deeds of one who does not believe in the Last Day, who hopes for no reward in them, and for whom there is no ultimate end to which they lead, are therefore annihilated and nullified.

{148} ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body that lowed.﴾ It was fashioned by al-Samiri, who cast into it a handful of dust from the footprint of the Messenger, so that it had a lowing, a sound. They worshipped it and took it as a god, and he said: "This is your god and the god of Musa, but Musa forgot." Musa went off to seek Him. This is from their foolishness and their lack of insight. How could the Lord of the earth and the heavens be confused for them with a calf, one of the most deficient of creatures? For this reason He said, explaining that it has none of the essential or active attributes that would require it to be a god: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them﴾, that is, and lack of speech is a great deficiency. They were in a better state than this animal or inanimate object that does not speak. ﴿Nor does it guide them to a way﴾, that is, it does not direct them to a religious path, nor does it secure for them any worldly benefit, because it is established in minds and natures that taking as a god one who neither speaks nor benefits nor harms is among the most absolute falsehood and the most repulsive folly. For this reason He said: ﴿They took it, and they were wrongdoers﴾, for they placed worship in other than its proper place, and associated with Allah what He had not sent down any authority for. In this there is evidence that whoever denies the speech of Allah has denied the divine attributes of Allah, exalted is He, because Allah mentioned that the absence of speech is evidence of the unfitness of that which does not speak for divinity.

{149} ﴿And when﴾ Musa returned to his people and found them in this state and informed them of their misguidance, they regretted, and ﴿they were overcome with remorse﴾, that is, from the distress and regret over their deed. ﴿And they saw that they had gone astray﴾, so they turned repentantly to Allah and humbled themselves before Him. ﴿They said: "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers,"﴾ those who have lost both this world and the Hereafter.

{150} ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾, that is, filled with anger and rage at them, due to the completeness of his jealousy for Allah, peace be upon him, and the perfection of his sincere counsel and compassion. ﴿He said: "Evil is what you have done in my absence after me."﴾ That is, evil is the state in which you have replaced me after my departure from you, for it is a state that leads to everlasting destruction and endless misery. ﴿Did you rush ahead of the command of your Lord?﴾ For He had promised you the descent of the Book, and you hastened with your corrupt opinion to this ugly act. ﴿And he threw down the tablets﴾, that is, he threw them down in anger. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head﴾, Harun, and by his beard, ﴿dragging him toward himself.﴾ He said to him: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Have you disobeyed my command?﴾ — referring to his words: ﴿Take my place among my people, act rightly, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.﴾ He said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."﴾ And his words here, ﴿son of my mother﴾, are a softening of his brother by mentioning only the mother, though he was his full brother, of the same mother and father. ﴿Indeed the people deemed me weak﴾, that is, they despised me when I said to them: "O my people, you are only being tested by this, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful; so follow me and obey my command." ﴿And they nearly killed me﴾, so do not think me negligent, ﴿so do not let the enemies gloat over me﴾ by your rebuking me and your harming me, for the enemies are eager to find in me a slip or to discover a fault in me. ﴿And do not place me with the wrongdoing people﴾, so that you would treat me as you treat them.

{151} Musa, peace be upon him, regretted what he had hastily done to his brother before knowing his innocence of the shortcoming he had suspected of him. He said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my brother﴾, Harun, ﴿and admit us into Your mercy﴾, that is, into its midst, and let Your mercy encompass us from every side, for it is an impregnable fortress against all evils, and in it is all goodness and joy. ﴿And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, that is, the most merciful toward us of every merciful one, more merciful toward us than our fathers, our mothers, our children, and ourselves.

{152} Allah, exalted is He, said, explaining the condition of the people of the calf who worshipped it: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾, that is, as a god, ﴿will receive wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world﴾, just as they angered their Lord and treated His command with contempt. ﴿And thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾. Every fabricator against Allah is a liar concerning His law, attributing to Him what He has not said. He will have a share of the wrath of Allah and of humiliation in the life of this world.

{153} The wrath of Allah had indeed befallen them when He commanded them to kill themselves, and that Allah would not be pleased with them except by that. So some of them killed others, and the battle ended with many slain. Then Allah relented toward them afterward. For this reason He mentioned a general ruling that they and others are included in, saying: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds﴾, of polytheism, major sins, and minor sins, ﴿and then repented after them﴾, by regretting what had passed, ceasing from them, and resolving not to return to them, ﴿and believed﴾ in Allah and in what Allah has made obligatory to believe in. Faith is not complete except with the actions of the hearts and the actions of the limbs that follow from faith. ﴿Indeed your Lord, after them﴾, that is, after this state, the state of repentance from evil deeds and return to acts of obedience, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, who forgives sins and erases them, even if they were as great as the earth's expanse, ﴿and Merciful﴾ in accepting repentance and granting success in acts of goodness and in accepting them.

{154} ﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa﴾, that is, his anger calmed and his soul returned to composure, and he recognized his situation, he occupied himself with the most important matters to him. So he took ﴿the tablets﴾ that he had thrown down, which were tablets of great size and magnificence, ﴿and in their inscription﴾, that is, containing and comprising, ﴿guidance and mercy﴾. That is, in them is guidance from error, the clarification of truth from falsehood, good actions and evil actions, guidance toward the best deeds, morals, and etiquettes, and mercy and felicity for whoever acts by them and knows their rulings and meanings. However, not everyone accepts the guidance and mercy of Allah; rather, it is accepted and submitted to, and received with acceptance, ﴿by those who fear their Lord﴾, that is, who are apprehensive of Him and stand in awe of Him. As for one who does not fear Allah or the standing before Him, he will only increase in arrogance and aversion through them, and the proof of Allah will be established against him by them.

{155} ﴿And Musa chose﴾ from among them ﴿seventy men﴾ from their best, that they might make excuses for their people before their Lord, and Allah appointed them a time at which they would present themselves. When they arrived, they said: "O Musa! Show us Allah openly!" They were so bold toward Allah with great audacity, and they behaved badly toward Him. So ﴿the thunderbolt seized them﴾, and they fell dead. Musa, peace be upon him, continued to humble himself before Allah and to devote himself, saying: ﴿My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me as well.﴾ That is, before they came, when they would have been in a state in which they could make excuses to their people. They have become the wrongdoers. ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾ That is, the weak of intellect and feeble of judgment. He humbled himself before Allah and made his excuse that those who were bold against Allah do not possess complete intellects to restrain them from what they said and did, and that a trial had befallen them by which a person is troubled and fears for the loss of his religion. He said: ﴿It is but Your trial; You send astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers.﴾ That is, You are the best to forgive, the most worthy to show mercy, and the most generous in giving and bestowing favour. It is as if Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O my Lord, the primary aim for all of us is to adhere to Your obedience and to believe in You, and that whoever is possessed of intellect and right guidance and remains upon what You have bestowed upon him of success will never cease to be upright. As for one whose intellect has weakened, whose judgment has become foolish, and whom trial has diverted, it is for these two reasons that he has done what he did. Yet, You are the Most Merciful of the merciful and the best of forgivers, so forgive us and have mercy upon us!" Allah answered his request, brought them back to life after their death, and forgave them their sins.

{156} Musa said, completing his supplication: ﴿And write for us in this world good﴾, of beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and righteous deeds, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ good, which is what Allah has prepared for His righteous friends of reward. ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, that is, we have returned, acknowledging our shortcomings and turning penitently in all our affairs. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted is He: ﴿My punishment I afflict with whom I will,﴾ of those who were wretched and exposed themselves to its causes, ﴿but My mercy encompasses all things﴾, of the upper and lower worlds, the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever. There is no creature except that the mercy of Allah has reached it and His bounty and kindness have overwhelmed it. But the special mercy that entails felicity in this world and the Hereafter is not for everyone. For this reason He said of it: ﴿So I will write it for those who fear Allah﴾, from sins, minor and major, ﴿and who give zakat﴾, the obligatory zakat, to its deserving recipients, ﴿and who believe in Our signs.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 7, verses 103–171 (part 3 of 3):

**Verse 157:** Complete faith in the signs of God includes knowing their meaning and acting in accordance with them. Among this is following the Prophet (ﷺ) outwardly and inwardly, in the foundations of the religion (usul) and its branches (furu').

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered﴾: This is a qualification that distinguishes him from the other prophets. The intended person is Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and the context concerns the condition of the Children of Israel. Belief in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is a condition for their entry into faith, and those who believe in him and follow him are the people of the absolute mercy that God has prescribed for them. He is described as "unlettered" because he was from the Arabs, an unlettered nation that could neither read nor write, and before the Qur'an they had no scripture.

﴿Whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾: By his name and his description, the greatest and most glorious of which is that he calls to what is good and forbids what is evil. ﴿He enjoins on them what is good﴾: That is, everything recognized as good, righteous and beneficial, namely *ma'ruf* (what is known and accepted as good). ﴿And forbids them what is evil﴾: That is, everything recognized as ugly by reason and natural disposition, namely *munkar* (what is denounced as wrong). So he commands them to pray, to give zakat, to fast, to make the pilgrimage, to maintain family ties, to be dutiful to parents, to be kind to neighbors and to slaves, to benefit all creatures, to be truthful, chaste, righteous, sincere in counsel, and similar things. He forbids associating partners with God, unjustly killing souls, fornication, drinking what intoxicates the mind, oppressing any creature, lying, immorality, and the like. The greatest proof that he is the Messenger of God is what he calls to, commands, forbids, and what he makes lawful and unlawful. He makes lawful the good things, namely foods, drinks and marriages, ﴿and makes unlawful for them the foul things﴾, namely foods, drinks, marriages, sayings and actions.

﴿And relieves them of their burdens and the shackles that were upon them﴾: That is, among his attributes is that his religion is easy, tolerant and facilitated, with no heavy burden, no shackles, no hardships and no weighty obligations.

﴿So those who believe in him and honor him﴾: That is, glorify and revere him, ﴿and support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him﴾: This is the Qur'an, by which one is guided through the darkness of doubt and ignorance, and which is followed when opinions conflict. ﴿Those are the successful﴾: Those who attain the good of this world and the Hereafter, and are saved from the evil of both, because they have taken the greatest means of success. As for one who does not believe in this unlettered Prophet, does not honor and support him, and does not follow the light that was sent down with him, those are the losers.

**Verse 158:** When he called the People of the Torah among the Children of Israel to follow him, and it might have been supposed that the ruling was limited to them, he gave a statement indicating generality. He said: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾: That is, to your Arabs and non-Arabs, to the People of the Book among you and to others. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: He disposes of them by His universal decrees, His sovereign arrangements, and His legislative rulings in religion. Among these is that He sent to you a great Messenger who calls you to God and to the abode of His honor, and warns you against everything that distances you from Him and from the abode of His honor. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾: That is, there is no one worthy of worship except God alone, without partner, and His worship is known only through His messengers. ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾: That is, among His arrangements are giving life and causing death, in which no one shares with Him. God made death a bridge and a passage through which one crosses to the abode of permanence. Whoever believes in that abode certainly affirms the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾: Belief in the heart, including the actions of the heart and the limbs, ﴿who believes in God and His words﴾: That is, believe in this Messenger, who is upright in his beliefs and actions. ﴿And follow him that you may be guided﴾: In your religious and worldly interests, for if you do not follow him, you will go far astray.

**Verse 159:** ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾: That is, a group, ﴿who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾: That is, they guide people by teaching them and giving them rulings, and they establish justice among them in judging their disputes, as God says: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾.

In this there is a virtue for the community of Moses (peace be upon him), and that God made among them guides who guide by His command. It seems that the mention of this noble verse is a kind of qualification of what came before. God mentioned earlier a number of the defects of the Children of Israel that contradict perfection and oppose guidance, so one might suppose that this applies to all of them. Therefore He mentioned that among them is an upright group, guiding and guided.

**Verse 160:** ﴿And We divided them﴾: That is, We separated them, ﴿into twelve tribes, as nations﴾: That is, twelve known and bonded tribes, each son of Jacob's sons forming a tribe. ﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾: That is, they asked him to supplicate God to provide water for them to drink and for their livestock to drink. This was because, God knows best, they were in a place with little water. God revealed to Moses, in response to their request: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. It may be a specific rock, or it may be a generic noun including any rock. He struck it, ﴿and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾: That is, from that rock flowed twelve flowing springs. ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾: That is, He apportioned to each of the twelve tribes a spring, so they knew it, were reassured, and rested from exhaustion and crowding. This was part of God's complete favor to them. ﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾: So that it protected them from the heat of the sun. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna﴾: Which is a sweet food, ﴿and quail﴾: Which is the meat of a bird, among the finest and most delicious kinds of birds. God combined for them shade, drink, and good food, both sweets and meats, in a manner of comfort and tranquility. It was said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, ﴿and they did not wrong Us﴾: When they did not thank God and did not do what God had made obligatory upon them. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾: Since they deprived themselves of all good and exposed themselves to evil and retribution. This continued for the duration of their wandering in the wilderness (*tih*, the desert of wandering).

**Verse 161:** ﴿And when it was said to them: Dwell in this town﴾: That is, enter it to be your homeland and dwelling, and it is Iliya (Jerusalem). ﴿And eat from it wherever you wish﴾: That town had many trees, abundant fruits, and a comfortable life, so God commanded them to eat from it wherever they wanted. ﴿And say: Hittah (remove our burden)﴾: When you enter the gate. That is: remove our sins from us and pardon us. ﴿And enter the gate prostrating﴾: That is, humbled before your Lord, submissive to His might and grateful for His blessing. So He commanded them to humble themselves and seek forgiveness, and promised them in return the forgiveness of their sins and both immediate and deferred reward. He said: ﴿We will forgive you your sins; We will increase the doers of good﴾: In the good of this world and the Hereafter.

**Verse 162:** ﴿But those who wronged among them did not comply with this command from God. Rather, they changed the word that had been said to them﴾: That is, they disobeyed God and treated His command lightly. ﴿They said a word other than what was said to them﴾: Instead of asking for forgiveness and saying *hittah*, they said *habbah fi sha'irah* (a grain in barley). If they changed the word, despite its ease and simplicity, then changing the action is all the more so. For this reason they entered crawling on their buttocks. ﴿So We sent upon them﴾: When they opposed God's command and disobeyed Him, ﴿a punishment from the sky﴾: That is, severe torment, either plague or another heavenly punishment. God did not wrong them in punishing them, but that happened ﴿because they were wronging.﴾

**Verse 163:** ﴿And ask them﴾: That is, ask the Children of Israel ﴿about the town which was by the sea﴾: That is, on its shore, during the time of their transgression and God's punishment upon them, ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾: God had commanded them to glorify and respect it and not to hunt on it. God tested and examined them, so the fish would come to them on their Sabbath day in great numbers, floating on the surface of the sea. ﴿And on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, it did not come to them﴾: That is, when the Sabbath day had passed, it would go away into the sea so they saw nothing of it. ﴿Thus did We test them because they were defiantly disobedient﴾: Their defiance is what required God to test them and subject them to this trial. Had they not been defiant, God would have spared them and would not have exposed them to trial and evil.

**Verse 164:** They devised ways to hunt, digging pits for the fish and setting up nets. When the fish came on the Sabbath and fell into those pits and nets, they did not take them on that day, but when Sunday came, they took them. This became widespread among them, and they split into three groups. Most of them transgressed, dared, and declared it openly. One group declared its prohibition and denounced them. A third group was content with the denunciation of the others and their admonition to them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ It is as if they were saying: there is no benefit in admonishing those who have violated God's sanctities and have not listened to advice, but persisted in transgression and defiance, for God will surely punish them, either by destruction or severe torment. The admonishers responded: ﴿We do so as a clear excuse to your Lord﴾: That is, so that we may be excused regarding them, ﴿and perhaps they will fear God﴾: That is, abandon the disobedience they are engaged in. We do not despair of their guidance, for perhaps the admonition will benefit them and the blame will affect them. This is the greatest purpose of forbidding evil: to serve as an excuse and to establish proof against the one who is commanded and forbidden, and perhaps God will guide him to act in accordance with that command and prohibition.

**Verse 165:** ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: That is, they abandoned what they had been reminded of and persisted in their error and transgression. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾: This is God's custom with His servants: when punishment descends, those who enjoin good and forbid evil are saved. ﴿And We seized those who wronged﴾: Those who transgressed on the Sabbath ﴿with a wretched punishment﴾: That is, severe, ﴿because they were defiantly disobedient﴾.

As for the other group that said to the admonishers, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy﴾, the commentators differ about whether they were saved or destroyed. The apparent view is that they were among the saved, for God restricted destruction to the wrongdoers, and He did not mention that they were wrongdoers. This indicates that punishment was specific to those who transgressed on the Sabbath. Also, enjoining good and forbidding evil is a *fard kifayah* (communal obligation): if some do it, it is dropped from the others, so they were content with the denunciation of those others. Furthermore, they denounced them by saying: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ Thus they showed, in their anger at them, what indicates that they strongly disliked their action and that God would punish them with the most severe punishment.

**Verse 166:** ﴿So when they became arrogant regarding what they were forbidden﴾: That is, they were hardened and did not soften or take heed. ﴿We said to them﴾: A *qadari* (decreed, by divine power) statement: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾. So they became apes by God's permission, and God removed them far from His mercy.

**Verse 167:** Then He mentioned the imposition of humiliation and degradation upon those who remained of them, saying: ﴿And when your Lord declared﴾: That is, announced explicitly, ﴿that He would surely send upon them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with a wretched punishment﴾: That is, humiliate and degrade them. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment﴾: For whoever disobeys Him, so that He hastens the punishment for him in this world. ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: For whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him; He forgives his sins, covers his faults, and shows mercy by accepting his good deeds and rewarding him with various kinds of reward. God did to them what He had promised them, so they remain in humiliation and abasement under the rule of others. No banner is raised for them, and no standard is victorious for them.

**Verse 168:** ﴿And We divided them throughout the earth into nations﴾: That is, We scattered and dispersed them throughout the earth after they had been united. ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾: Those who uphold the rights of God and the rights of His servants. ﴿And among them are others less than that﴾: That is, below righteousness: either moderate, or those who wrong themselves. ﴿And We tested them﴾: According to Our custom and practice, ﴿with good and bad﴾: That is, with ease and hardship, ﴿that they might return﴾: From the ruin in which they persisted, and return to the guidance for which they were created. They continued among the righteous, the wicked, and the moderate.

**Verse 169:** Until there succeeded them ﴿a successor﴾: whose evil increased. ﴿They inherited﴾: after them ﴿the Scripture﴾, and the reference for it became them. They dealt with it according to their desires, bribes were offered to them so that they would issue rulings and judge unjustly, and bribery spread among them. ﴿They take the goods of this lower world and say﴾: acknowledging that it is a sin and that they are wrongdoers: ﴿It will be forgiven us﴾. This statement is devoid of reality, for it is not true repentance or a genuine request for forgiveness. Had it been so, they would have regretted what they did and resolved never to return to it. But whenever another offer or another bribe came to them, they took it. Thus they ﴿exchanged the signs of God for a small price﴾, and ﴿exchanged that which is lower for that which is better.﴾ God said, rebuking them and declaring their audacity: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them, that they would not say about God except the truth?﴾ So why do they say about Him other than the truth, following their desires and inclining toward their greed? ﴿And they had studied what is in it﴾: So there was no confusion for them regarding it. Rather, they undertook their affair deliberately and were fully aware of their affair. This is greater in sin, more deserving of blame, and more grave in punishment. This arises from deficiency of their intellect and foolishness of their judgment, in preferring the life of this world to the Hereafter. For this reason He said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear God﴾: That is, the forbidden things God prohibited for them, such as foods that are obtained and eaten as bribes for judging other than what God revealed, and other kinds of prohibited things. ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾: That is, will you not have intellects that weigh what should be preferred against what should be sacrificed, and what is more worthy of pursuit and of being prioritized over others? The essence of reason is to consider consequences. As for one who looks to a fleeting, cut-off, immediate gain that forfeits a great and lasting bliss, how can he have reason or judgment?

**Verse 170:** The truly wise are those whom God described with His words: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Scripture﴾: That is, adhere to it in knowledge and action, knowing what it contains of rulings and reports, the knowledge of which is the most noble of sciences, and acting upon its commands, which are the delight of the eyes, the joy of hearts, the happiness of souls, and the welfare of this world and the Hereafter. Among the most important of the commanded acts that must be held fast is establishing the prayer, outwardly and inwardly. For this reason He singled it out for mention, because of its excellence and nobility, and because it is the scale of faith and its establishment calls to the establishment of other acts of worship. Since all their work was reform, God said: ﴿Indeed, We do not let go to waste the reward of the reformers﴾: In their words, deeds and intentions, reforming themselves and others.

This verse and those like it show that God sent His messengers, peace be upon them, with righteousness and not corruption, with benefits and not harms, and that they were sent with the welfare of both abodes. Therefore whoever is more righteous is closer to following them.

**Verse 171:** Then God said: ﴿And when We lifted the mountain over them﴾: When they refused to accept what was in the Torah, God obligated them to act, and He lifted the mountain above their heads so that it became above them, ﴿as though it were a canopy, and they thought it was about to fall upon them﴾. It was said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾: That is, with determination and striving. ﴿And remember what is in it﴾: By studying, discussing, and characterizing oneself with acting upon it, ﴿that you may fear God﴾: If you do that.

{103} That is: then after those messengers We sent Musa (Moses), the speaker with God (al-Kalim), the great imam and the noble messenger, to a people who were haughty and tyrannical, namely Pharaoh and his chiefs, from among their nobles and great ones. We showed them the great signs of God, the like of which had never been witnessed. {But they wronged them}: by not submitting to their truth, for whoever does not submit to it is a wrongdoer; rather, they were arrogant toward them. {So see how was the end of the corrupters}: how God destroyed them and made them follow in this world with blame and curse, and on the Day of Resurrection, how evil is the gift that is given.

{104} This is a summary which he explained with His saying: {Musa said}: when he came to Pharaoh calling him to faith: {O Pharaoh, I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds}; that is: I am a messenger from a great Sender, who is the Lord of the worlds, encompassing the upper and lower worlds, the Nurturer of all His creation through various divine arrangements, among which is that He does not leave them neglected, but sends to them messengers as bearers of good news and warners. He is the One whom no one can dare to presume upon by claiming that He sent him when He did not send him.

{105} Since this is His state, and He has chosen me and singled me out for His message, it is incumbent upon me not to lie against Him or say about Him anything except the truth; for if I said otherwise, He would hasten punishment upon me and seize me with the seizing of the Mighty, the Powerful. This necessitates that they submit to him and follow him, especially since he has come to them with a clear proof from God confirming the truth of what he brought. It was therefore obligatory upon them to act upon the purpose of his message, which has two great aims: their faith in him and their following of him, and the sending of the Children of Israel, the people whom God preferred over the worlds, the descendants of the prophets and the lineage of Ya'qub (Jacob), peace be upon him, of whom Musa, peace and blessings be upon him, is one.

{106} Pharaoh said to him: {If you have come with a sign, then produce it, if you are among the truthful}.

{107} {So Musa cast} his staff {down}: upon the earth, {and behold, it was a clearly visible serpent}; that is: a manifest snake moving swiftly while they were watching it.

{108} {And he drew out} his hand from his collar {and behold, it was white to the observers}: without any defect. These are two great signs indicating the truth of what Musa brought and his sincerity, and that he is the messenger of the Lord of the worlds.

{109} But those who do not believe, even if every sign came to them, they would not believe until they see the painful punishment. Therefore {the chiefs of the people of Pharaoh said}, when what they saw of the signs overwhelmed them and they still did not believe, and sought corrupt interpretations for them: {Indeed, this is a skilled magician}; that is: adept in his sorcery.

{110} Then they frightened the weak-minded and foolish by saying that he {intends} with this deed {to expel you from your land}; that is: he wants to drive you out of your homelands. {So what do you advise?} That is: they consulted among themselves about what to do with Musa and what would avert their harm, in their own estimation; for what he brought, if it is not countered by something that nullifies and refutes it, then it will enter the minds of most people.

{111–112} Then their opinion settled, and they said to Pharaoh: {Put him and his brother off}; that is: detain them and delay them, and send into the cities people who will gather the inhabitants of the realm and bring every skilled sorcerer; that is: bring the expert magicians to confront what Musa brought. They said: O Musa, {Appoint for us and for you a meeting place which neither we nor you will fail to keep, in an open place}. He said: {Your appointment is the Day of Adornment, and that the people be gathered in the forenoon}. So Pharaoh withdrew, gathered his plan, and then came.

{113} And He said here: {The sorcerers came to Pharaoh}, seeking reward if they prevailed, and said: {Indeed, for us there will surely be a reward if we are the victors}.

{114} Pharaoh said: {Yes}: there will be a reward for you, {and indeed you will be among those brought near}. He promised them reward, nearness, and high rank with him, so that they would strive and exert their utmost effort in contending with Musa.

{115} When they were present with Musa in the presence of the great multitude, {they said}, in a tone of arrogance and indifference to what Musa had brought: {O Musa, either you cast, or we will be the ones who cast}.

{116} Musa said: {Cast}, so that the people might see what they had and what Musa had. {When they cast} their ropes and staffs, behold, by their sorcery they appeared to be serpents moving swiftly. They {bewitched the eyes of the people, terrified them, and produced a great sorcery}: the like of which had not been found in magic.

{117} {And We revealed to Musa: Cast your staff}; so he cast it, {and behold, it swallowed up what they falsely showed}; that is: what they lied about and made appear otherwise.

{118} {So the truth was established}; that is: it became clear, manifest, and made known in that assembly, {and what they had been doing was nullified}.

{119} {So they were overcome there}; that is: in that place, {and they turned back humiliated}; that is: abased, their falsehood having been annihilated and their sorcery having vanished, and they did not attain the aim they had expected.

{120–122} Those who were most clearly shown the great truth were the people of skill and sorcery, who know of the kinds and details of magic what others do not know. They recognized that this was a great sign from the signs of God, against which no one has any power. So {the sorcerers fell down prostrate}. {They said: We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Musa and Harun}; that is: we affirm what Musa was sent with of clear signs.

{123} Pharaoh said to them, threatening them for their faith: {Have you believed in him before I gave you permission?} The wicked man was an autocratic ruler over bodies and speech; it had been firmly established in his mind and theirs that his word was obeyed and his command was binding upon them, and that no one could go beyond his word and rule. In such a condition, nations decline, their minds and influence weaken, and they become unable to defend their rights. Therefore God said of him: {So he made his people light-minded, and they obeyed him}. And here he said: {Have you believed in him before I gave you permission?}; that is: this is a breach of manners on your part and an insolence toward me. Then he deceived his people and said: {Indeed, this is a plot you have plotted in the city, to expel its people from it}; that is: Musa is your chief who taught you magic, and you agreed with him that you would be defeated by him so that he would appear, and you would follow him, and then the people or most of them would follow you, and you would expel its people from it. This is a lie, which he himself knows, as does anyone who examines the circumstances: Musa, peace be upon him, had not met with any of them, they had been gathered according to the opinion of Pharaoh and his envoys, what Musa brought was a divine sign, and the sorcerers had exerted their utmost effort in contending with Musa until they were defeated and the truth became clear to them, so they followed it. Then Pharaoh threatened them, saying: {Soon you will know} what punishment will befall you.

{124} {I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides}: the wicked man claimed that they were corrupters on earth, and he would do to them what is done to corrupters: cutting off the hands and feet on opposite sides; that is: the right hand and the left foot. {Then I will crucify you} on the trunks of palm trees, so that you may be disgraced in his estimation, {all of you}; that is: I will not do this to one person and not another, but all of you will taste this punishment.

{125} The sorcerers who believed said to Pharaoh when he threatened them: {Indeed, to our Lord we will return}; that is: we do not care about your punishment, for God is better and more enduring; so decree what you will decree.

{126} {And you do not resent us} for anything, that is: you do not blame us for denying us and threatening us; we have no sin {except that we believed in the signs of our Lord when they came to us}. If this is a sin for which one is blamed and deserves punishment, then it is our sin. Then they called upon God to make them firm and steadfast, and they said: {Our Lord, pour upon us patience}; that is: abundantly, as the indefiniteness indicates, because this is a great trial that leads to the loss of life, so much patience is needed in it, that the heart may be steadied and the believer may be at peace in his faith, and the great anxiety may leave him. {And cause us to die as Muslims}; that is: submitting to Your command and following Your messenger. Apparently, Pharaoh did carry out what he had threatened, and God made them steadfast in faith.

{127} Then Pharaoh, his chiefs, and their common people who followed the chiefs, became arrogant toward the signs of God and denied them wrongfully and haughtily, and they said to Pharaoh, inciting him to act against Musa and claiming that what he brought was falsehood and corruption: {Will you leave Musa and his people to corrupt the land?}; by calling to God and to noble character and good deeds, which are righteousness on earth, while what they themselves were upon was corruption. But the wrongdoers do not care what they say. {And leave you and your gods}; that is: leave you and your gods, and forbid you, and turn people away from following you. Pharaoh answered them, saying that he would leave the Children of Israel with Musa in a state in which they would not increase, and Pharaoh and his people, in his estimation, would be safe from their harm: {We will kill their sons and spare their women}; that is: we will let the women live and not kill them; for if we do that, we will be secure from their multiplication, and we will keep the rest of them as servants and make them labor at whatever tasks we wish. {And indeed we are over them, dominant}: there is no escape for them from our rule and no power. This is the extreme of Pharaoh's tyranny, arrogance, and cruelty.

{128} Musa said {to his people}, advising them, in this state in which they had no power or ability to resist, to seek divine support and the help of the Lord: {Seek help in God}; that is: rely upon Him to bring what benefits you and to repel what harms you, and trust that God will complete your affair. {And be patient}; that is: keep to patience in what befalls you, awaiting relief. {Indeed, the earth belongs to God}: it is not Pharaoh's nor his people's that they should control it. {He bequeaths it to whom He wills of His servants}; that is: He alternates it among people according to His will and wisdom. But the final outcome is for the righteous, for even if they are tested for a period by God's trial and wisdom, victory is theirs, {and the final outcome}, the praiseworthy one, is for them over their people. This is the duty of the servant: when he has power, to take the means that repel harm from himself and others as far as he can; and when he is powerless, to be patient, seek God's help, and await relief.

{129} They said to Musa, impatient at how long they had remained under Pharaoh's torment and harm: {We were harmed before you came to us}, for they had been subjecting us to the worst torment, slaughtering our sons and sparing our women, {and after you came to us}, likewise. Musa said to them, giving them hope of relief and deliverance from their evil: {Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land}; that is: He will establish you in it and give you the management of it, {and see how you will act}: whether you will be thankful or ungrateful. This is a promise which God fulfilled when the time He willed came.

{130} God, the Exalted, said, explaining how He dealt with the family of Pharaoh during this final period, that this is His custom and practice with nations: that He seizes them {with misfortune and adversity, that they may humble themselves} and the verses that follow: {And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of drought}; that is: with periods of barrenness and famine, {and loss of fruits, that they might take heed}; that is: that they might be admonished that what befell and struck them was a reproof from God to them, perhaps they would turn back from their disbelief. But it did not benefit them nor was it of use; rather, they persisted in wrongdoing and corruption.

{131} {But when good came to them}; that is: fertility and abundance of provision, {they said: This is ours}; that is: we deserve it, and so they did not thank God for it. {And if evil afflicted them}; that is: drought and famine, {they ascribed their misfortune to Musa and those with him}; that is: they said: it came upon us because of the coming of Musa and the following of the Children of Israel after him. God said: {Indeed, their omen is with God}; that is: by His decree and power, not as they said; rather, their sins and disbelief are the cause of it. Rather, most of them do not know; that is: this is why they said what they said.

{132} {And they said}, clarifying to Musa that they would not cease nor depart from their falsehood: {Whatever sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will not believe you}; that is: it has been established with us that you are a sorcerer; so whatever sign you bring, we are certain it is sorcery, and we will not believe or accept you. This is the utmost of obstinacy, that the disbelievers reach a point where circumstances are equal to them, whether signs descend upon them or not.

{133} {So We sent upon them the flood}; that is: abundant water that drowned their trees and crops and caused them great harm, {and the locusts}: which devoured their fruits, crops, and plants, {and the lice}: it was said that it is the small locust; and apparently it is the well-known louse, {and the frogs}: which filled their vessels, disturbed them, and harmed them severely, {and the blood}: either it was nosebleeds, or as many commentators said: their water which they drank turned into blood, so they drank nothing but blood and cooked nothing but with blood. {As distinct signs}; that is: proofs and clear evidence that they were liars and wrongdoers, and that what Musa brought is true and right. {But they were arrogant}: when they saw the signs, {and they were}: in their former affair {a criminal people}: therefore God punished them by leaving them in error and misguidance.

{134} {When the punishment befell them}; that is: the torment. It may be that what is meant by it is the plague, as many commentators said; and it may be that what is meant is what preceded: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, for they are a punishment and torment; and whenever one of them struck them, {they said: O Musa, pray to your Lord for us by what He has covenanted with you}; that is: they sought intercession through Musa by what God had entrusted to him of revelation and law. {If you remove the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you and send the Children of Israel with you}. They were liars in this, having no aim except the removal of the torment that had befallen them, and they thought that once it was lifted nothing else would befall them.

{135} {But when We removed the punishment from them for a term which they were to reach}; that is: until a period which God had decreed for their survival, and it was not a permanent removal but a temporary one, {behold, they broke their word}: the covenant they had made with Musa, promising to believe in him and send the Children of Israel. They neither believed in him nor sent the Children of Israel with him, but persisted in their disbelief, wandering blindly, and in torturing the Children of Israel relentlessly.

{136} {So We took retribution upon them}; that is: when the appointed time for their destruction came, God commanded Musa to journey by night with the Children of Israel and informed him that Pharaoh and his armies would pursue them. {Then Pharaoh sent into the cities gatherers} to assemble people to pursue the Children of Israel, and they said to them: {Indeed, these are but a small band. And indeed, they have enraged us. And indeed, we are a vigilant host. So We expelled them from gardens and springs, and treasures and a noble station. Thus, and We caused the Children of Israel to inherit them. So they pursued them at sunrise. And when the two groups saw each other, the companions of Musa said: Indeed, we are overtaken. He said: No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me. So We revealed to Musa: Strike the sea with your staff; and it parted, and each part was like a great mountain. And We brought the others near to that place. And We saved Musa and those with him, all of them. Then We drowned the others.} And here He said: {So We drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them}; that is: because of their denial of God's signs and their turning away from the truth that they indicated.

{137} {And We caused to inherit the people who had been oppressed}: in the land; that is: the Children of Israel, who had been servants to the family of Pharaoh, who had subjected them to the worst torment. God caused them to inherit {the eastern and western parts of the earth}. The earth meant here is the land of Egypt, in which they had been oppressed and humiliated; that is: God gave them dominion over all of it and established them in it, {which We had blessed, and the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience}, when Musa said to them: {Seek help in God and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to God; He bequeaths it to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous}. {And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been building}: of the enormous structures and the elaborate dwellings, {and what they had been erecting}. Those are their houses, [ruined] because they did wrong. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who know.

{138} ﴿And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea.﴾ After Allah had delivered them from their enemy Pharaoh and his people, and Allah had destroyed them while the Children of Israel were watching, ﴿they came upon a people devoted to idols of their own﴾, that is, they stayed beside them, sought blessing from them, and worshipped them. Out of their ignorance and foolishness, and after Allah had shown them the signs that He had shown them, they said to their prophet Musa: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ That is, legislate for us that we may take idols as gods, as these people have taken them. Musa said to them: ﴿Indeed you are a people who act in ignorance.﴾ What ignorance is greater than ignorance of one's Lord and Creator? He wanted to equate with Him others who possess no power to benefit or harm, nor to cause death, life, or resurrection!

{139} For this reason Musa said to them: ﴿Indeed, these people are doomed in what they are engaged in, and worthless is what they have been doing.﴾ This is because their calling upon them is worthless, and they themselves are worthless. So the action is worthless and its end is worthless.

{140} ﴿He said: "Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, while He has preferred you over the worlds?"﴾ That is, shall I seek for you a god other than Allah, the One worthy of worship, perfect in His essence, attributes, and actions? ﴿And He has preferred you over the worlds.﴾ This requires that you respond to His favour and preference with gratitude, which means singling Allah out alone for worship and disbelieving in whatever is called upon besides Him.

{141} Then he reminded them of the blessing Allah had bestowed upon them, saying: ﴿And [remember] when We delivered you from the people of Pharaoh﴾, that is, from Pharaoh and his household, ﴿who inflicted upon you the worst torment﴾, that is, who subjected you to the most severe of punishments, namely that they slaughtered ﴿your sons and spared your women﴾. ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, that is, deliverance from their torment was a magnificent blessing and an abundant gift; or, in that torment they inflicted upon you was a great trial from your Lord upon you.

{142} When Musa reminded them and admonished them, they desisted from that. When Allah had completed His blessing upon them by delivering them from their enemy and establishing them in the land, He, blessed and exalted, willed to complete His blessing upon them by sending down the Book containing the legal rulings (ahkam shar'iyyah) and the acceptable beliefs (aqa'id). So He appointed to Musa thirty nights, and completed them with ten, so they became forty nights. This was so that Musa might prepare and make himself ready for the promise of Allah, and that its descent would have a great place in their hearts and they would long for it. When Musa went to the appointed time of his Lord, he said to Harun, enjoining him concerning the Children of Israel out of his concern for them and compassion toward them: ﴿Take my place among my people﴾, that is, be my successor among them and act among them as I used to act. ﴿And act rightly﴾, that is, follow the path of righteousness. ﴿And do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾, who are those who engage in sins.

{143} ﴿And when Musa came at Our appointed time﴾, which We had set for him for the descent of the Book, ﴿and his Lord spoke to him﴾, by speaking to him with His revelation, His command, and His prohibition, his soul yearned to see Allah, and his self was stirred toward that out of love for his Lord and affection for seeing Him. So ﴿he said: "My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look upon You."﴾ Allah said: ﴿You will not see Me﴾, that is, you will not be able now to see Me. Indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, created creation in this abode in a constitution by which they cannot bear and cannot remain steadfast to see Allah. There is no evidence in this that they will not see Him in Paradise. The Qur'anic texts and the prophetic hadith have established that the people of Paradise will see their Lord, blessed and exalted, and will delight in gazing upon His noble Face, and that He will create them in a perfect constitution by which they will be able to see Allah, exalted is He. For this reason Allah, in this verse, made seeing Him conditional upon the firmness of the mountain, so He said, persuading Musa not to be granted his request: ﴿But look at the mountain; if it remains in its place﴾, that is, when Allah manifests Himself to it, ﴿then you will see Me.﴾ ﴿So when his Lord manifested Himself to the mountain﴾, the solid, massive one, ﴿He made it crumble to dust﴾, that is, it collapsed like sand, in alarm at the sight of Allah and its inability to remain steadfast. ﴿And Musa fell unconscious﴾ when he saw what he saw. Then it became clear to him that if the mountain could not remain steady before the sight of Allah, Musa was even less able to remain steady. He sought forgiveness from his Lord for what had come from him of the request that was not fitting for its place. He said: ﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, I declare You far exalted above and magnify You beyond what is unworthy of Your majesty. ﴿I have repented to You﴾ from all sins and from any lack of good manners toward You. ﴿And I am the first of the believers﴾, that is, peace and blessings be upon him, renewed his faith by what Allah perfected for him of what he had been ignorant of before that.

{144} When Allah prevented him from seeing Him after he had been longing for it, He gave him abundant good. He said: ﴿O Musa, indeed I have chosen you over the people﴾, that is, I have selected you, chosen you, preferred you, and singled you out with great virtues and noble distinctions, ﴿by My messages﴾, which I do not assign nor single out except to the most excellent of creation, ﴿and by My speech﴾ to you without intermediary. This is a virtue in which Musa was singled out, the one known among his brother messengers as al-Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah). ﴿So take what I have given you﴾ of the blessings, and take what I have given you of commands and prohibitions with an open breast, and receive it with acceptance and submission. ﴿And be among the grateful﴾ to Allah for what He has singled you out for and preferred you with.

{145} ﴿And We wrote for him on the tablets concerning all things﴾ that people need, ﴿an admonition﴾ that inclines souls toward acts of goodness and deters them from acts of evil, ﴿and a detailed explanation of all things﴾ of the legal rulings, beliefs, morals, and etiquettes. ﴿So take them with strength﴾, that is, with earnestness and diligence in establishing them. ﴿And enjoin your people to take the best of them﴾, which are the obligatory and recommended commands, for these are the best of them. In this there is evidence that Allah's commands in every law are complete, just, and good. ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾, after Allah destroyed them and left their dwellings as a lesson for those after them, by which the rightly guided, humble believers may take heed.

{146} As for others, He said concerning them: ﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾, that is, from taking heed of the signs of the horizons and of the self, and from understanding the verses of the Book, ﴿those who are arrogant upon the earth without right﴾, that is, who act arrogantly toward the servants of Allah, toward the truth, and toward the one who brought it. Whoever has this characteristic, Allah deprives him of abundant good and forsakes him, and he does not understand from the signs of Allah that which would benefit him. Indeed, realities may be inverted for him and he may come to regard ugliness as beautiful. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾, because of their aversion, their opposition, and their hostility toward Allah and His Messenger. ﴿And if they see the way of right guidance﴾, that is, guidance and uprightness, which is the path that leads to Allah and to the abode of His honour, ﴿they will not take it as a way﴾, that is, they will not follow it nor desire it. ﴿And if they see the way of error﴾, that is, the misguidance that leads its companion to the abode of misery, ﴿they will take it as a way.﴾ The cause of their deviation into this deviation is: ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾. Their rejection of the signs of Allah, their heedlessness of what they are intended to convey, and their contempt for them is what caused them to follow the path of error and abandon the path of right guidance, with what that necessitated.

{147} ﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾, the great ones indicating the truth of what We sent Our messengers with, ﴿and the meeting of the Hereafter﴾, ﴿their deeds have become worthless﴾, because they were not founded on a basis, and their condition, which is faith in the signs of Allah and belief in His recompense, was lacking. ﴿Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ That is, in the nullification of their deeds and the attainment of the opposite of their intended aims. For the deeds of one who does not believe in the Last Day, who hopes for no reward in them, and for whom there is no ultimate end to which they lead, are therefore annihilated and nullified.

{148} ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him, from their ornaments a calf, a body that lowed.﴾ It was fashioned by al-Samiri, who cast into it a handful of dust from the footprint of the Messenger, so that it had a lowing, a sound. They worshipped it and took it as a god, and he said: "This is your god and the god of Musa, but Musa forgot." Musa went off to seek Him. This is from their foolishness and their lack of insight. How could the Lord of the earth and the heavens be confused for them with a calf, one of the most deficient of creatures? For this reason He said, explaining that it has none of the essential or active attributes that would require it to be a god: ﴿Did they not see that it does not speak to them﴾, that is, and lack of speech is a great deficiency. They were in a better state than this animal or inanimate object that does not speak. ﴿Nor does it guide them to a way﴾, that is, it does not direct them to a religious path, nor does it secure for them any worldly benefit, because it is established in minds and natures that taking as a god one who neither speaks nor benefits nor harms is among the most absolute falsehood and the most repulsive folly. For this reason He said: ﴿They took it, and they were wrongdoers﴾, for they placed worship in other than its proper place, and associated with Allah what He had not sent down any authority for. In this there is evidence that whoever denies the speech of Allah has denied the divine attributes of Allah, exalted is He, because Allah mentioned that the absence of speech is evidence of the unfitness of that which does not speak for divinity.

{149} ﴿And when﴾ Musa returned to his people and found them in this state and informed them of their misguidance, they regretted, and ﴿they were overcome with remorse﴾, that is, from the distress and regret over their deed. ﴿And they saw that they had gone astray﴾, so they turned repentantly to Allah and humbled themselves before Him. ﴿They said: "If our Lord does not have mercy upon us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers,"﴾ those who have lost both this world and the Hereafter.

{150} ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾, that is, filled with anger and rage at them, due to the completeness of his jealousy for Allah, peace be upon him, and the perfection of his sincere counsel and compassion. ﴿He said: "Evil is what you have done in my absence after me."﴾ That is, evil is the state in which you have replaced me after my departure from you, for it is a state that leads to everlasting destruction and endless misery. ﴿Did you rush ahead of the command of your Lord?﴾ For He had promised you the descent of the Book, and you hastened with your corrupt opinion to this ugly act. ﴿And he threw down the tablets﴾, that is, he threw them down in anger. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head﴾, Harun, and by his beard, ﴿dragging him toward himself.﴾ He said to him: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me? Have you disobeyed my command?﴾ — referring to his words: ﴿Take my place among my people, act rightly, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.﴾ He said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe my word."﴾ And his words here, ﴿son of my mother﴾, are a softening of his brother by mentioning only the mother, though he was his full brother, of the same mother and father. ﴿Indeed the people deemed me weak﴾, that is, they despised me when I said to them: "O my people, you are only being tested by this, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful; so follow me and obey my command." ﴿And they nearly killed me﴾, so do not think me negligent, ﴿so do not let the enemies gloat over me﴾ by your rebuking me and your harming me, for the enemies are eager to find in me a slip or to discover a fault in me. ﴿And do not place me with the wrongdoing people﴾, so that you would treat me as you treat them.

{151} Musa, peace be upon him, regretted what he had hastily done to his brother before knowing his innocence of the shortcoming he had suspected of him. He said: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my brother﴾, Harun, ﴿and admit us into Your mercy﴾, that is, into its midst, and let Your mercy encompass us from every side, for it is an impregnable fortress against all evils, and in it is all goodness and joy. ﴿And You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾, that is, the most merciful toward us of every merciful one, more merciful toward us than our fathers, our mothers, our children, and ourselves.

{152} Allah, exalted is He, said, explaining the condition of the people of the calf who worshipped it: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾, that is, as a god, ﴿will receive wrath from their Lord and humiliation in the life of this world﴾, just as they angered their Lord and treated His command with contempt. ﴿And thus do We recompense the fabricators﴾. Every fabricator against Allah is a liar concerning His law, attributing to Him what He has not said. He will have a share of the wrath of Allah and of humiliation in the life of this world.

{153} The wrath of Allah had indeed befallen them when He commanded them to kill themselves, and that Allah would not be pleased with them except by that. So some of them killed others, and the battle ended with many slain. Then Allah relented toward them afterward. For this reason He mentioned a general ruling that they and others are included in, saying: ﴿And those who committed evil deeds﴾, of polytheism, major sins, and minor sins, ﴿and then repented after them﴾, by regretting what had passed, ceasing from them, and resolving not to return to them, ﴿and believed﴾ in Allah and in what Allah has made obligatory to believe in. Faith is not complete except with the actions of the hearts and the actions of the limbs that follow from faith. ﴿Indeed your Lord, after them﴾, that is, after this state, the state of repentance from evil deeds and return to acts of obedience, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, who forgives sins and erases them, even if they were as great as the earth's expanse, ﴿and Merciful﴾ in accepting repentance and granting success in acts of goodness and in accepting them.

{154} ﴿And when the anger subsided from Musa﴾, that is, his anger calmed and his soul returned to composure, and he recognized his situation, he occupied himself with the most important matters to him. So he took ﴿the tablets﴾ that he had thrown down, which were tablets of great size and magnificence, ﴿and in their inscription﴾, that is, containing and comprising, ﴿guidance and mercy﴾. That is, in them is guidance from error, the clarification of truth from falsehood, good actions and evil actions, guidance toward the best deeds, morals, and etiquettes, and mercy and felicity for whoever acts by them and knows their rulings and meanings. However, not everyone accepts the guidance and mercy of Allah; rather, it is accepted and submitted to, and received with acceptance, ﴿by those who fear their Lord﴾, that is, who are apprehensive of Him and stand in awe of Him. As for one who does not fear Allah or the standing before Him, he will only increase in arrogance and aversion through them, and the proof of Allah will be established against him by them.

{155} ﴿And Musa chose﴾ from among them ﴿seventy men﴾ from their best, that they might make excuses for their people before their Lord, and Allah appointed them a time at which they would present themselves. When they arrived, they said: "O Musa! Show us Allah openly!" They were so bold toward Allah with great audacity, and they behaved badly toward Him. So ﴿the thunderbolt seized them﴾, and they fell dead. Musa, peace be upon him, continued to humble himself before Allah and to devote himself, saying: ﴿My Lord, had You willed, You could have destroyed them before, and me as well.﴾ That is, before they came, when they would have been in a state in which they could make excuses to their people. They have become the wrongdoers. ﴿Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?﴾ That is, the weak of intellect and feeble of judgment. He humbled himself before Allah and made his excuse that those who were bold against Allah do not possess complete intellects to restrain them from what they said and did, and that a trial had befallen them by which a person is troubled and fears for the loss of his religion. He said: ﴿It is but Your trial; You send astray by it whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of forgivers.﴾ That is, You are the best to forgive, the most worthy to show mercy, and the most generous in giving and bestowing favour. It is as if Musa, peace be upon him, said: "O my Lord, the primary aim for all of us is to adhere to Your obedience and to believe in You, and that whoever is possessed of intellect and right guidance and remains upon what You have bestowed upon him of success will never cease to be upright. As for one whose intellect has weakened, whose judgment has become foolish, and whom trial has diverted, it is for these two reasons that he has done what he did. Yet, You are the Most Merciful of the merciful and the best of forgivers, so forgive us and have mercy upon us!" Allah answered his request, brought them back to life after their death, and forgave them their sins.

{156} Musa said, completing his supplication: ﴿And write for us in this world good﴾, of beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and righteous deeds, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ good, which is what Allah has prepared for His righteous friends of reward. ﴿Indeed, we have turned back to You﴾, that is, we have returned, acknowledging our shortcomings and turning penitently in all our affairs. ﴿He said﴾, Allah, exalted is He: ﴿My punishment I afflict with whom I will,﴾ of those who were wretched and exposed themselves to its causes, ﴿but My mercy encompasses all things﴾, of the upper and lower worlds, the righteous and the wicked, the believer and the disbeliever. There is no creature except that the mercy of Allah has reached it and His bounty and kindness have overwhelmed it. But the special mercy that entails felicity in this world and the Hereafter is not for everyone. For this reason He said of it: ﴿So I will write it for those who fear Allah﴾, from sins, minor and major, ﴿and who give zakat﴾, the obligatory zakat, to its deserving recipients, ﴿and who believe in Our signs.﴾

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 7, verses 103–171 (part 3 of 3):

**Verse 157:** Complete faith in the signs of God includes knowing their meaning and acting in accordance with them. Among this is following the Prophet (ﷺ) outwardly and inwardly, in the foundations of the religion (usul) and its branches (furu').

﴿Those who follow the Messenger, the Prophet, the unlettered﴾: This is a qualification that distinguishes him from the other prophets. The intended person is Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and the context concerns the condition of the Children of Israel. Belief in the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) is a condition for their entry into faith, and those who believe in him and follow him are the people of the absolute mercy that God has prescribed for them. He is described as "unlettered" because he was from the Arabs, an unlettered nation that could neither read nor write, and before the Qur'an they had no scripture.

﴿Whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾: By his name and his description, the greatest and most glorious of which is that he calls to what is good and forbids what is evil. ﴿He enjoins on them what is good﴾: That is, everything recognized as good, righteous and beneficial, namely *ma'ruf* (what is known and accepted as good). ﴿And forbids them what is evil﴾: That is, everything recognized as ugly by reason and natural disposition, namely *munkar* (what is denounced as wrong). So he commands them to pray, to give zakat, to fast, to make the pilgrimage, to maintain family ties, to be dutiful to parents, to be kind to neighbors and to slaves, to benefit all creatures, to be truthful, chaste, righteous, sincere in counsel, and similar things. He forbids associating partners with God, unjustly killing souls, fornication, drinking what intoxicates the mind, oppressing any creature, lying, immorality, and the like. The greatest proof that he is the Messenger of God is what he calls to, commands, forbids, and what he makes lawful and unlawful. He makes lawful the good things, namely foods, drinks and marriages, ﴿and makes unlawful for them the foul things﴾, namely foods, drinks, marriages, sayings and actions.

﴿And relieves them of their burdens and the shackles that were upon them﴾: That is, among his attributes is that his religion is easy, tolerant and facilitated, with no heavy burden, no shackles, no hardships and no weighty obligations.

﴿So those who believe in him and honor him﴾: That is, glorify and revere him, ﴿and support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him﴾: This is the Qur'an, by which one is guided through the darkness of doubt and ignorance, and which is followed when opinions conflict. ﴿Those are the successful﴾: Those who attain the good of this world and the Hereafter, and are saved from the evil of both, because they have taken the greatest means of success. As for one who does not believe in this unlettered Prophet, does not honor and support him, and does not follow the light that was sent down with him, those are the losers.

**Verse 158:** When he called the People of the Torah among the Children of Israel to follow him, and it might have been supposed that the ruling was limited to them, he gave a statement indicating generality. He said: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾: That is, to your Arabs and non-Arabs, to the People of the Book among you and to others. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: He disposes of them by His universal decrees, His sovereign arrangements, and His legislative rulings in religion. Among these is that He sent to you a great Messenger who calls you to God and to the abode of His honor, and warns you against everything that distances you from Him and from the abode of His honor. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾: That is, there is no one worthy of worship except God alone, without partner, and His worship is known only through His messengers. ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾: That is, among His arrangements are giving life and causing death, in which no one shares with Him. God made death a bridge and a passage through which one crosses to the abode of permanence. Whoever believes in that abode certainly affirms the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾: Belief in the heart, including the actions of the heart and the limbs, ﴿who believes in God and His words﴾: That is, believe in this Messenger, who is upright in his beliefs and actions. ﴿And follow him that you may be guided﴾: In your religious and worldly interests, for if you do not follow him, you will go far astray.

**Verse 159:** ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾: That is, a group, ﴿who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾: That is, they guide people by teaching them and giving them rulings, and they establish justice among them in judging their disputes, as God says: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾.

In this there is a virtue for the community of Moses (peace be upon him), and that God made among them guides who guide by His command. It seems that the mention of this noble verse is a kind of qualification of what came before. God mentioned earlier a number of the defects of the Children of Israel that contradict perfection and oppose guidance, so one might suppose that this applies to all of them. Therefore He mentioned that among them is an upright group, guiding and guided.

**Verse 160:** ﴿And We divided them﴾: That is, We separated them, ﴿into twelve tribes, as nations﴾: That is, twelve known and bonded tribes, each son of Jacob's sons forming a tribe. ﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾: That is, they asked him to supplicate God to provide water for them to drink and for their livestock to drink. This was because, God knows best, they were in a place with little water. God revealed to Moses, in response to their request: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. It may be a specific rock, or it may be a generic noun including any rock. He struck it, ﴿and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾: That is, from that rock flowed twelve flowing springs. ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾: That is, He apportioned to each of the twelve tribes a spring, so they knew it, were reassured, and rested from exhaustion and crowding. This was part of God's complete favor to them. ﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾: So that it protected them from the heat of the sun. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna﴾: Which is a sweet food, ﴿and quail﴾: Which is the meat of a bird, among the finest and most delicious kinds of birds. God combined for them shade, drink, and good food, both sweets and meats, in a manner of comfort and tranquility. It was said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, ﴿and they did not wrong Us﴾: When they did not thank God and did not do what God had made obligatory upon them. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾: Since they deprived themselves of all good and exposed themselves to evil and retribution. This continued for the duration of their wandering in the wilderness (*tih*, the desert of wandering).
