﴿And relieves them of their burdens and the shackles that were upon them﴾: That is, among his attributes is that his religion is easy, tolerant and facilitated, with no heavy burden, no shackles, no hardships and no weighty obligations.

﴿So those who believe in him and honor him﴾: That is, glorify and revere him, ﴿and support him, and follow the light that was sent down with him﴾: This is the Qur'an, by which one is guided through the darkness of doubt and ignorance, and which is followed when opinions conflict. ﴿Those are the successful﴾: Those who attain the good of this world and the Hereafter, and are saved from the evil of both, because they have taken the greatest means of success. As for one who does not believe in this unlettered Prophet, does not honor and support him, and does not follow the light that was sent down with him, those are the losers.

**Verse 158:** When he called the People of the Torah among the Children of Israel to follow him, and it might have been supposed that the ruling was limited to them, he gave a statement indicating generality. He said: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of God to you all﴾: That is, to your Arabs and non-Arabs, to the People of the Book among you and to others. ﴿To whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾: He disposes of them by His universal decrees, His sovereign arrangements, and His legislative rulings in religion. Among these is that He sent to you a great Messenger who calls you to God and to the abode of His honor, and warns you against everything that distances you from Him and from the abode of His honor. ﴿There is no deity except Him﴾: That is, there is no one worthy of worship except God alone, without partner, and His worship is known only through His messengers. ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾: That is, among His arrangements are giving life and causing death, in which no one shares with Him. God made death a bridge and a passage through which one crosses to the abode of permanence. Whoever believes in that abode certainly affirms the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿So believe in God and His Messenger, the unlettered Prophet﴾: Belief in the heart, including the actions of the heart and the limbs, ﴿who believes in God and His words﴾: That is, believe in this Messenger, who is upright in his beliefs and actions. ﴿And follow him that you may be guided﴾: In your religious and worldly interests, for if you do not follow him, you will go far astray.

**Verse 159:** ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community﴾: That is, a group, ﴿who guide by the truth and by it establish justice﴾: That is, they guide people by teaching them and giving them rulings, and they establish justice among them in judging their disputes, as God says: ﴿And We made them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and used to be certain of Our signs﴾.

In this there is a virtue for the community of Moses (peace be upon him), and that God made among them guides who guide by His command. It seems that the mention of this noble verse is a kind of qualification of what came before. God mentioned earlier a number of the defects of the Children of Israel that contradict perfection and oppose guidance, so one might suppose that this applies to all of them. Therefore He mentioned that among them is an upright group, guiding and guided.

**Verse 160:** ﴿And We divided them﴾: That is, We separated them, ﴿into twelve tribes, as nations﴾: That is, twelve known and bonded tribes, each son of Jacob's sons forming a tribe. ﴿And We revealed to Moses when his people asked him for water﴾: That is, they asked him to supplicate God to provide water for them to drink and for their livestock to drink. This was because, God knows best, they were in a place with little water. God revealed to Moses, in response to their request: ﴿Strike the rock with your staff﴾. It may be a specific rock, or it may be a generic noun including any rock. He struck it, ﴿and there gushed forth from it twelve springs﴾: That is, from that rock flowed twelve flowing springs. ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾: That is, He apportioned to each of the twelve tribes a spring, so they knew it, were reassured, and rested from exhaustion and crowding. This was part of God's complete favor to them. ﴿And We shaded them with clouds﴾: So that it protected them from the heat of the sun. ﴿And We sent down upon them manna﴾: Which is a sweet food, ﴿and quail﴾: Which is the meat of a bird, among the finest and most delicious kinds of birds. God combined for them shade, drink, and good food, both sweets and meats, in a manner of comfort and tranquility. It was said to them: ﴿Eat of the good things We have provided for you﴾, ﴿and they did not wrong Us﴾: When they did not thank God and did not do what God had made obligatory upon them. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾: Since they deprived themselves of all good and exposed themselves to evil and retribution. This continued for the duration of their wandering in the wilderness (*tih*, the desert of wandering).

**Verse 161:** ﴿And when it was said to them: Dwell in this town﴾: That is, enter it to be your homeland and dwelling, and it is Iliya (Jerusalem). ﴿And eat from it wherever you wish﴾: That town had many trees, abundant fruits, and a comfortable life, so God commanded them to eat from it wherever they wanted. ﴿And say: Hittah (remove our burden)﴾: When you enter the gate. That is: remove our sins from us and pardon us. ﴿And enter the gate prostrating﴾: That is, humbled before your Lord, submissive to His might and grateful for His blessing. So He commanded them to humble themselves and seek forgiveness, and promised them in return the forgiveness of their sins and both immediate and deferred reward. He said: ﴿We will forgive you your sins; We will increase the doers of good﴾: In the good of this world and the Hereafter.

**Verse 162:** ﴿But those who wronged among them did not comply with this command from God. Rather, they changed the word that had been said to them﴾: That is, they disobeyed God and treated His command lightly. ﴿They said a word other than what was said to them﴾: Instead of asking for forgiveness and saying *hittah*, they said *habbah fi sha'irah* (a grain in barley). If they changed the word, despite its ease and simplicity, then changing the action is all the more so. For this reason they entered crawling on their buttocks. ﴿So We sent upon them﴾: When they opposed God's command and disobeyed Him, ﴿a punishment from the sky﴾: That is, severe torment, either plague or another heavenly punishment. God did not wrong them in punishing them, but that happened ﴿because they were wronging.﴾

**Verse 163:** ﴿And ask them﴾: That is, ask the Children of Israel ﴿about the town which was by the sea﴾: That is, on its shore, during the time of their transgression and God's punishment upon them, ﴿when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾: God had commanded them to glorify and respect it and not to hunt on it. God tested and examined them, so the fish would come to them on their Sabbath day in great numbers, floating on the surface of the sea. ﴿And on the day they did not observe the Sabbath, it did not come to them﴾: That is, when the Sabbath day had passed, it would go away into the sea so they saw nothing of it. ﴿Thus did We test them because they were defiantly disobedient﴾: Their defiance is what required God to test them and subject them to this trial. Had they not been defiant, God would have spared them and would not have exposed them to trial and evil.

**Verse 164:** They devised ways to hunt, digging pits for the fish and setting up nets. When the fish came on the Sabbath and fell into those pits and nets, they did not take them on that day, but when Sunday came, they took them. This became widespread among them, and they split into three groups. Most of them transgressed, dared, and declared it openly. One group declared its prohibition and denounced them. A third group was content with the denunciation of the others and their admonition to them, and said: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ It is as if they were saying: there is no benefit in admonishing those who have violated God's sanctities and have not listened to advice, but persisted in transgression and defiance, for God will surely punish them, either by destruction or severe torment. The admonishers responded: ﴿We do so as a clear excuse to your Lord﴾: That is, so that we may be excused regarding them, ﴿and perhaps they will fear God﴾: That is, abandon the disobedience they are engaged in. We do not despair of their guidance, for perhaps the admonition will benefit them and the blame will affect them. This is the greatest purpose of forbidding evil: to serve as an excuse and to establish proof against the one who is commanded and forbidden, and perhaps God will guide him to act in accordance with that command and prohibition.

**Verse 165:** ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾: That is, they abandoned what they had been reminded of and persisted in their error and transgression. ﴿We saved those who forbade evil﴾: This is God's custom with His servants: when punishment descends, those who enjoin good and forbid evil are saved. ﴿And We seized those who wronged﴾: Those who transgressed on the Sabbath ﴿with a wretched punishment﴾: That is, severe, ﴿because they were defiantly disobedient﴾.

As for the other group that said to the admonishers, ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy﴾, the commentators differ about whether they were saved or destroyed. The apparent view is that they were among the saved, for God restricted destruction to the wrongdoers, and He did not mention that they were wrongdoers. This indicates that punishment was specific to those who transgressed on the Sabbath. Also, enjoining good and forbidding evil is a *fard kifayah* (communal obligation): if some do it, it is dropped from the others, so they were content with the denunciation of those others. Furthermore, they denounced them by saying: ﴿Why do you admonish a people whom God is going to destroy or punish with a severe punishment?﴾ Thus they showed, in their anger at them, what indicates that they strongly disliked their action and that God would punish them with the most severe punishment.

**Verse 166:** ﴿So when they became arrogant regarding what they were forbidden﴾: That is, they were hardened and did not soften or take heed. ﴿We said to them﴾: A *qadari* (decreed, by divine power) statement: ﴿Be apes, despised﴾. So they became apes by God's permission, and God removed them far from His mercy.

**Verse 167:** Then He mentioned the imposition of humiliation and degradation upon those who remained of them, saying: ﴿And when your Lord declared﴾: That is, announced explicitly, ﴿that He would surely send upon them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with a wretched punishment﴾: That is, humiliate and degrade them. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment﴾: For whoever disobeys Him, so that He hastens the punishment for him in this world. ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: For whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him; He forgives his sins, covers his faults, and shows mercy by accepting his good deeds and rewarding him with various kinds of reward. God did to them what He had promised them, so they remain in humiliation and abasement under the rule of others. No banner is raised for them, and no standard is victorious for them.

**Verse 168:** ﴿And We divided them throughout the earth into nations﴾: That is, We scattered and dispersed them throughout the earth after they had been united. ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾: Those who uphold the rights of God and the rights of His servants. ﴿And among them are others less than that﴾: That is, below righteousness: either moderate, or those who wrong themselves. ﴿And We tested them﴾: According to Our custom and practice, ﴿with good and bad﴾: That is, with ease and hardship, ﴿that they might return﴾: From the ruin in which they persisted, and return to the guidance for which they were created. They continued among the righteous, the wicked, and the moderate.

**Verse 169:** Until there succeeded them ﴿a successor﴾: whose evil increased. ﴿They inherited﴾: after them ﴿the Scripture﴾, and the reference for it became them. They dealt with it according to their desires, bribes were offered to them so that they would issue rulings and judge unjustly, and bribery spread among them. ﴿They take the goods of this lower world and say﴾: acknowledging that it is a sin and that they are wrongdoers: ﴿It will be forgiven us﴾. This statement is devoid of reality, for it is not true repentance or a genuine request for forgiveness. Had it been so, they would have regretted what they did and resolved never to return to it. But whenever another offer or another bribe came to them, they took it. Thus they ﴿exchanged the signs of God for a small price﴾, and ﴿exchanged that which is lower for that which is better.﴾ God said, rebuking them and declaring their audacity: ﴿Was not the covenant of the Scripture taken from them, that they would not say about God except the truth?﴾ So why do they say about Him other than the truth, following their desires and inclining toward their greed? ﴿And they had studied what is in it﴾: So there was no confusion for them regarding it. Rather, they undertook their affair deliberately and were fully aware of their affair. This is greater in sin, more deserving of blame, and more grave in punishment. This arises from deficiency of their intellect and foolishness of their judgment, in preferring the life of this world to the Hereafter. For this reason He said: ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who fear God﴾: That is, the forbidden things God prohibited for them, such as foods that are obtained and eaten as bribes for judging other than what God revealed, and other kinds of prohibited things. ﴿Will you not then use reason?﴾: That is, will you not have intellects that weigh what should be preferred against what should be sacrificed, and what is more worthy of pursuit and of being prioritized over others? The essence of reason is to consider consequences. As for one who looks to a fleeting, cut-off, immediate gain that forfeits a great and lasting bliss, how can he have reason or judgment?

**Verse 170:** The truly wise are those whom God described with His words: ﴿And those who hold fast to the Scripture﴾: That is, adhere to it in knowledge and action, knowing what it contains of rulings and reports, the knowledge of which is the most noble of sciences, and acting upon its commands, which are the delight of the eyes, the joy of hearts, the happiness of souls, and the welfare of this world and the Hereafter. Among the most important of the commanded acts that must be held fast is establishing the prayer, outwardly and inwardly. For this reason He singled it out for mention, because of its excellence and nobility, and because it is the scale of faith and its establishment calls to the establishment of other acts of worship. Since all their work was reform, God said: ﴿Indeed, We do not let go to waste the reward of the reformers﴾: In their words, deeds and intentions, reforming themselves and others.

This verse and those like it show that God sent His messengers, peace be upon them, with righteousness and not corruption, with benefits and not harms, and that they were sent with the welfare of both abodes. Therefore whoever is more righteous is closer to following them.

**Verse 171:** Then God said: ﴿And when We lifted the mountain over them﴾: When they refused to accept what was in the Torah, God obligated them to act, and He lifted the mountain above their heads so that it became above them, ﴿as though it were a canopy, and they thought it was about to fall upon them﴾. It was said to them: ﴿Take what We have given you with strength﴾: That is, with determination and striving. ﴿And remember what is in it﴾: By studying, discussing, and characterizing oneself with acting upon it, ﴿that you may fear God﴾: If you do that.

{172–173} He, exalted is He, says: {And when your Lord took from the Children of Adam, from their loins, their offspring}; that is, He brought forth their offspring from their backs, and made them reproduce and multiply generation after generation. {And} when He brought them forth from the wombs of their mothers and the loins of their fathers, {He made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?"}; that is, He established them in acknowledging His lordship through what He placed in their natural disposition (fitrah) of affirming that He is their Lord, their Creator and their Sovereign. They said: "Yes, we testify." For indeed God, exalted is He, created His servants upon the upright, true religion (al-din al-hanif al-qayyim), so every person is created upon that; but the natural disposition may be changed and altered by what befalls the minds and by corrupt beliefs. Therefore {they said, "Yes, we testify." Lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, "Indeed, we were unaware of this."}; that is, We tested you so that you would acknowledge what is established among you, that God, exalted is He, is your Lord, lest you deny it on the Day of Resurrection, refuse to acknowledge anything of that, and claim that the proof of God was not established against you and that you had no knowledge of it, but rather you were heedless and negligent of it. So today your argument has been cut off, and the conclusive proof of God is established against you. Or you may argue with another proof, saying: {Only our fathers associated partners with God before, and we were offspring after them. Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?}: so we followed their example and followed them in their falsehood. Yet God has placed in your natural disposition that which guides you to know that what your fathers held is false, and that the truth is what the messengers brought. This confronts what you found your fathers upon and overcomes it. Indeed, it may happen to a servant that from the sayings of his misguided fathers and their corrupt doctrines there appears to him to be the truth; and this is only due to his turning away from the proofs of God, His clear signs and His signs in the horizons and in the self. So his turning away from that and his inclination toward what the falsifiers say may bring him to a state in which he prefers falsehood over truth.

This is the correct interpretation of these verses. It has been said that this refers to the day when God took the covenant from the offspring of Adam, when He brought them out of his back and made them testify concerning themselves, and they testified to that, and He thereby argued against them with what He had commanded them at that time, for their wrongdoing in their disbelief and obstinacy in this world and the Hereafter. But there is nothing in the verse that indicates this, nor is it fitting to it, nor does the wisdom of God require it, and reality bears witness to that. For this covenant and pledge which they mentioned, that it was when God brought forth the offspring of Adam from his back while they were in a world like tiny atoms, is something no one remembers, and it does not come to the mind of any human being. So how would God argue against them with a matter of which they have no knowledge, no existence, and no trace?!

{174} Therefore, since this was a clear and manifest matter, He, exalted is He, said: {And thus We detail the signs}; that is, We make them clear and explain them, {so that they may return}: to what God placed in their natural dispositions and to what they pledged to God, so that they would refrain from ugly deeds.

**{175}** Almighty God says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿And recite to them the news of him to whom We gave Our verses﴾; meaning: We taught him [the knowledge of] the Book of God, so he became a great scholar and a learned authority. ﴿But he withdrew from them﴾; meaning: he withdrew from genuine attainment of knowledge of God's verses. For knowledge of them makes its possessor characterized by noble character and excellent deeds, and raises him to the highest ranks and the loftiest stations. But he cast this Book of God behind his back, rejected the morals that the Book enjoins, and stripped them off as one strips off a garment. ﴿So Satan pursued him﴾; meaning: he gained power over him when he came out of the impregnable fortress and descended to the lowest of the low. So he incited him to sins with full incitement. ﴿And he became of those who go astray﴾: having been formerly one of the rightly guided and the guides.

**{176}** This is because God abandoned him and left him to himself. Therefore God says: ﴿Had We willed, We would have elevated him thereby﴾; meaning: by enabling him to act upon them, so that he would be raised in this world and the next, and would be protected from his enemies. ﴿But he inclined to the earth﴾; meaning: he inclined to the base desires and worldly aims, ﴿and followed his desire﴾, and abandoned obedience to his Master.

﴿So his example is like the example of a dog: if you attack him he pants, or if you leave him he pants﴾; meaning: he is always panting in every state. Likewise, this man never ceases to be greedy, a greed that cuts his heart off from everything, and nothing of this world can satisfy his need. ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our verses﴾, after God had brought them to them, yet they did not submit to them, but rather denied them and rejected them, out of their own baseness before God and their following of their desires without guidance from God. ﴿So relate the stories that perhaps they will reflect﴾: upon the coining of examples, and upon lessons and signs. For when they reflect, they will know; and when they know, they will act.

**{177}** ﴿Evil is the example of the people who denied Our verses and were wronging themselves﴾; meaning: evil and ugly is the example of one who denies God's verses and wrongs himself through various kinds of sins, for their example is an evil example.

It is possible that what is meant by ﴿him to whom We gave Our verses﴾ is a specific person of whom what God mentioned came to pass, and God related his story as a warning to the servants. It is also possible that what is meant is a generic noun, encompassing everyone to whom God gave His verses and who then withdrew from them.

In these verses there is encouragement to act upon knowledge, and that this is an elevation from God for its possessor and a protection from Satan; and there is warning against failing to act upon it, and that this is a descent to the lowest of the low and an empowering of Satan over him. In them also is the point that following desire and inclining of the servant toward base pleasures becomes a cause of abandonment by God.

**{178}** Then God, Exalted, said, explaining that He alone guides and misguides: ﴿Whomever God guides﴾, by enabling him to do good, protecting him from what is hateful, and teaching him what he did not know, ﴿he is the truly guided﴾, because he preferred God's guidance. ﴿And whomever He sends astray﴾, by abandoning him and not enabling him to do good, ﴿those are the losers﴾ for their own selves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, that is the manifest loss.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 179:

{179} He, may He be exalted, says, explaining the great number of those who go astray, the misguided who follow the accursed Iblis: ﴿And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind﴾; that is, We brought them into being and spread them out. ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾; that is, no understanding or knowledge reaches them, except the mere establishment of proof. ﴿And they have eyes with which they do not see﴾: [they do not see] what would benefit them; rather, they have lost its benefit and its use. ﴿And they have ears with which they do not hear﴾: [they do not hear] in a way whose meaning reaches their hearts. ﴿Those are like livestock﴾; that is, those who possess these ugly characteristics are like the beasts that have lost their intellects, and these people preferred what perishes over what endures, so they were stripped of the distinctive quality of intellect. ﴿Rather, they are more astray﴾ than the beasts; for livestock are employed in what they were created for, and they have minds by which they perceive what harms them from what benefits them; therefore they are in a better condition than these people. And ﴿those are the heedless﴾: those who have neglected the most beneficial of things; they neglected faith in God, obedience to Him, and remembrance of Him. The hearts, hearing and sight were created for them to be a help in carrying out God's commands and rights, but they used them for the opposite of this purpose. Such people deserve to be among those whom God has created for Hell and made for it; they were created for the Fire and they work by the deeds of its people. As for those who employ these faculties in the worship of God, whose hearts are dyed with faith in God and love of Him, and who are not heedless of God, those are the people of Paradise, and they work by the deeds of the people of Paradise.

{180} This is an explanation of His great majesty and the breadth of His attributes, in that He has the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna). That is: for Him is every name that is beautiful. The governing principle is that every name indicates a great attribute of perfection, and it is for this reason that they are "beautiful." For if a name indicated no attribute but was a pure designation (ʿalam mahd), it would not be "beautiful"; likewise, if it indicated an attribute that is not an attribute of perfection, but rather either an attribute of deficiency or an attribute that is divided between praise and blame, it would not be "beautiful." Thus every one of His names indicates the entirety of the attribute from which it is derived, encompassing its whole meaning. Examples of this are: {Al-ʿAlim} (the All-Knowing), which indicates that He has comprehensive knowledge encompassing all things, so that not even the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heavens escapes His knowledge; {Al-Rahim} (the Especially Merciful), which indicates that He has great and vast mercy for everything; and {Al-Qadir} (the All-Powerful), which indicates that He has universal power that nothing can thwart... and similar names. And among the completeness of their being "beautiful" is that He is not called upon except by them. For this reason He said: {So call upon Him by them}. This includes both the supplication of worship (duʿa' al-ʿibadah) and the supplication of request (duʿa' al-masalah). So in every matter sought, one calls upon Him with what suits that matter. For example, the supplicant says: "O Allah, forgive me and have mercy upon me; indeed You are the All-Forgiving, the Most Merciful." And: "Accept my repentance, O Most Accepting of repentance!" And: "Provide for me, O Provider!" And: "Be gentle with me, O Gentle One!" And similar.

And His saying: {And leave those who deviate concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do}; that is, a punishment and torment for their deviation concerning His names. The reality of deviation (ilhad) is inclining the names away from that for which they were made, either by naming with them one who does not deserve them, such as the polytheists naming their deities with them; or by negating their meanings and distorting them, and making for them a meaning that neither Allah nor His Messenger intended; or by likening others to them. Therefore it is obligatory to beware of deviation concerning them and to beware of those who deviate concerning them. It is established in the Sahih, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Indeed, Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise."

{181} That is: and among those whom We have created is a community that is virtuous and complete in itself, perfecting others, guiding themselves and others by the truth. They know the truth, act upon it, teach it, and call to it and to acting by it. {And by it they act justly}: among people in their judgments when they judge concerning wealth, blood, rights, statements, and other matters. These are the imams of guidance (a'immat al-huda) and the lamps of darkness (masabih al-duja), and they are those whom Allah has blessed with faith, righteous deeds, mutual counsel to the truth, and mutual counsel to patience. They are the siddiqun (the truthful, those of the highest sincerity), whose rank comes right after the rank of prophethood. Among themselves they are of varying degrees, each according to his state and the elevation of his station. So glory be to Him who singles out for His mercy whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty.

{182} That is: "And those who denied Our signs" — the signs of Allah that indicate the truth of what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought of guidance — "and rejected them and did not accept them. {We will lead them step by step to destruction from where they do not know}": by granting them abundant provision.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah al-A'raf, verses 187–188:

{187} Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will be its appointed time?﴾ That is, those who deny you and seek to trap you ask: When is its appointed time, when will it come, and when will it descend upon creation? ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with my Lord﴾ That is, He, the Exalted, alone has exclusive knowledge of it. ﴿None will reveal it at its time except Him﴾ That is, none will make it manifest at its appointed time, the time decreed for it to occur, except Him. ﴿It has become heavy in the heavens and the earth﴾ That is, its knowledge is hidden from the people of the heavens and the earth, and its matter is also grave for them, so they are apprehensive of the Hour. ﴿It will not come to you except suddenly﴾ That is, unexpectedly, from where they do not perceive, without having prepared or readied themselves for it. ﴿They ask you as if you were well-informed about it﴾ That is, they are eager to ask you about the Hour as if you were intensely preoccupied with questioning about it, and they do not know that, because of the perfection of your knowledge of your Lord, and because you are indifferent to questions whose asking brings no benefit, you are neither eager for that [nor concerned with it, so why do they not follow your example and refrain from being preoccupied with this question] that is devoid of benefit and whose knowledge is unattainable. For no prophet sent nor any near angel knows it, and it is among the matters that He has concealed from creation, due to the perfection of His wisdom and the vastness of His knowledge. ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most people do not know﴾. Therefore they are eager for what they should not be eager for, especially like the condition of those who neglect asking about what is most important and leave aside the knowledge that is obligatory upon them, then turn to what no one has any way of comprehending and what they are not required to know.

{188} ﴿Say: I possess no power to benefit or harm myself﴾ For I am a poor, managed being; no good comes to me except from Allah, none repels evil from me except Him, and I have no knowledge except what Allah has taught me. ﴿And if I knew the unseen, I would have acquired much good, and no harm would have touched me﴾ That is, I would have adopted the means that I know produce for me benefits and advantages, and I would have guarded against everything that leads to evil and harm, through my knowledge of things before they occur and my knowledge of what they lead to. But because I lack such knowledge, what befalls me of evil may befall me, and what passes me of worldly benefits and advantages may pass me by. This is the clearest proof that I have no knowledge of the unseen. ﴿I am but a warner﴾ I warn of religious, worldly and otherworldly punishments, explain the deeds that lead to them, and caution against them; and I give glad tidings of immediate and deferred reward, by clarifying the deeds that lead to it and encouraging them. But not everyone accepts this glad tidings and warning; it is only the believers who benefit from it and accept it.

These noble verses clarify the ignorance of those who approach the Prophet (peace be upon him) and call upon him to obtain benefit or repel harm. He has no share in the matter whatsoever, and he cannot benefit one whom Allah has not benefited, nor repel harm from one from whom Allah has not repelled it; and he has no knowledge except what Allah [the Exalted] has taught him. He benefits only those who accept what he was sent with of glad tidings and warning and act upon it. This is the benefit of him, peace be upon him, which surpasses the benefit of fathers, mothers, friends and brothers, in that he urged the servants toward every good, warned them against every evil, and made it clear to them with the utmost explanation and elucidation.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 189–193:

{189} That is: {It is He who created you}, O men and women spread across the earth in your multitude and dispersal, {from a single soul}: and this is Adam, the father of mankind (ﷺ), {and made from it its mate}; that is, He created from Adam his wife, Eve, so that he might find rest in her. For since she was from him, there arose between them such affinity and harmony as calls for each of them to find rest in the other, and each was led to the other by the reins of desire. {Then when he covered her}; that is, when he enveloped her in intercourse, God decreed that offspring should come into being from that desire and that intercourse, and so she conceived {a light burden}, which is at the beginning of pregnancy, when the female does not feel it and it does not weigh on her. {Then when} it continued with her and {she became heavy} with it as it grew in her womb, then in their hearts there arose compassion for the child and concern for its coming forth alive, healthy and whole, free of any defect. So they called upon {God, their Lord, saying: If You give us} a child {righteous}; that is, sound in its creation, complete and without any deficiency, {we shall surely be among the thankful}.

{190} {Then when He gave them a righteous one}: in accordance with what they had asked, and the blessing upon them in it was complete, {they assigned partners to Him in what He had given them}; that is, they made partners with God in that child, whom God alone had brought into being, and the blessing of whom was His alone, and who gladdened the eyes of his parents. They made him a servant of other than God: either by naming him with a name meaning servant of other than God, such as Abd al-Harith, Abd al-'Uzza, Abd al-Ka'bah and the like, or by associating others with God in worship, after God had bestowed upon them blessings that no one among the servants can count. This is a transition from the particular to the general: the beginning of the discourse concerned Adam and Eve, and then it moved to speak of the species in general. There is no doubt that this is found widely among their descendants, and therefore God established against them the falsity of association, and that they are in this greatly unjust, the gravest of injustice, whether the association is in statements or in actions. For the One who created them from a single soul, who created from it its mate, who made for them mates from among themselves, then placed between them affection and mercy, so that some of them find rest in others, become attached to them and take pleasure in them, then guided them to that by which desire, pleasure, children and offspring are attained, then brought the offspring into being in the wombs of mothers for a set time for which their souls long, and they call upon God to bring it forth sound and healthy: God has completed His blessing upon them and granted them what they sought. Does He not then deserve to be worshipped, with no one associated with Him in His worship, and that they devote their religion sincerely to Him?!

{191–192} But the matter came about the opposite way: they associated with God {that which creates nothing and is itself created. And they cannot help them}; that is, their worshippers, {nor can they help themselves}. So if they create nothing, not even the weight of an atom, but are themselves created, and cannot ward off harm from those who worship them nor from themselves, then how can they be taken as gods alongside God?! This is nothing but the gravest injustice and the most profound folly.

{193} {And if you call them to guidance, they will not follow you; it is alike for you whether you call them or you remain silent}, O polytheists, these idols you worship besides God. So man is in a better state than they, for they neither hear nor see, neither guide nor are guided. All of this, when a discerning, intelligent person considers it in pure reflection, will decide with certainty the falsity of their divinity and the foolishness of those who worship them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verses 194–196:

{194} This is a form of challenge to the polytheists who worship idols. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you﴾; that is, there is no difference between you and them, for all of you are servants owned by Allah. So if you are truthful in your claim that they deserve some worship, ﴿then call upon them, and let them respond to you﴾, if you are truthful. If they respond to you and achieve what you seek, well and good; otherwise it becomes clear that you are liars in this claim, and that you have fabricated against Allah the greatest of falsehoods.

{195} This needs no clarification, for when you look at them you find their form indicating that they have no benefit whatsoever. They have no feet to walk with, no hands to strike with, no eyes to see with, and no ears to hear with. They lack all the faculties and powers present in a human being. If they do not respond when you call upon them, then they are servants like you, and indeed you are more complete than they are and stronger in many matters. So for what reason did you worship them?! ﴿Say: Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite﴾; that is, gather together, you and your partners, to inflict evil and harm upon me without delay or reprieve, for you are unable to inflict any harm upon me.

{196} Because my Protector is Allah, who takes charge of my affairs, bringing me benefits and warding off harms from me. ﴿He who has sent down the Book﴾: in which is guidance, healing and light, and this is part of His guardianship and His nurturing of His special servants in religion. ﴿And He takes charge of the righteous﴾: those whose intentions, deeds and words are sound. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah is the Protector of those who believe; He brings them out from darkness into light﴾. So the righteous believers, when they took their Lord as protector through faith and piety, and did not take as protectors others who neither benefit nor harm, Allah took them under His care, showed them kindness, helped them toward what is good and beneficial for them in their religion and their worldly life, and warded off from them every harm because of their faith; as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, Allah defends those who believe﴾.

(197–198) This also serves to show that these idols, which they worship besides Allah, do not deserve any part of worship, because they have no power or ability to help themselves or to help those who worship them, and they have no faculty of reason or of response. Were you to call them to guidance, they would not be guided. They are images with no life in them. You see them looking at you, yet they do not truly see, because they fashioned them in the likeness of living creatures, whether humans or others, and gave them eyes and limbs. When you look at them, you think they are alive; but when you examine them, you realize they are lifeless objects that do not move and have no life. So on what basis did the polytheists take them as gods alongside Allah? And for what benefit or profit did they remain devoted to them and draw near to them with all kinds of worship?

When this is understood, it becomes clear that the polytheists and the gods they worshipped, even if they all gathered together and wished to plot against the one whom the Creator of the heavens and the earth, the Guardian of the affairs of His righteous servants, has taken as protector, they would not be able to harm him in the least, owing to their complete impotence and the impotence of their gods, and owing to the perfect might and power of Allah and the strength of one who takes refuge in His majesty and relies upon Him.

It has also been said that the meaning of His words, {And you see them looking at you, yet they do not see}, is that the pronoun refers to the polytheists who denied the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So you think they are looking at you, O Messenger of Allah, with the gaze of contemplation by which the truthful is distinguished from the liar, but they do not perceive your reality and what those who discern signs perceive in you of beauty, perfection and truthfulness.

{199} This verse brings together good character toward people and what is fitting in dealing with them. What should be shown to people is: to take what is easy (al-'afw), that is, what their souls permit and what comes easily to them of deeds and character. So one does not burden them with what their natures do not allow. Rather, one thanks everyone for whatever good word or deed they show, or for less than that, overlooks their shortcomings and turns a blind eye to their faults, and does not look down on the young for being young, nor on the weak-minded for their lack of intelligence, nor on the poor for their poverty. Rather, one treats everyone with gentleness and with reciprocity as the situation requires and as will gladden their hearts. ﴿And enjoin what is good (al-'urf)﴾; that is, every good word, good deed and perfect character toward the near and the distant. So let what comes from you to people be either teaching knowledge, or urging toward good such as maintaining ties of kinship, or kindness to parents, or reconciling between people, or sincere beneficial advice, or sound judgment, or helping in righteousness and piety, or restraining from wrongdoing, or guiding to the attainment of a benefit, religious or worldly. Since harm from the ignorant is unavoidable, God Most High commanded that the ignorant be met with turning away from them and not meeting their ignorance with ignorance of one's own. So whoever harms you by word or deed, do not harm him; whoever withholds from you, do not withhold from him; whoever cuts you off, join with him; whoever wrongs you, be just toward him.

As for how the servant should deal with the devils of the jinn, God Most High said:

{200} That is: at any time and in any state. {If an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you} — that is, you sense from him whispering, discouragement from good, or urging toward evil and inciting to it — {then seek refuge in Allah}; that is, take shelter, hold fast to Allah, and seek protection in His sanctuary. For He is All-Hearing of what you say, {All-Knowing}: of your intention, your weakness, and the strength of your seeking refuge in Him. So He will protect you from his temptation and shield you from his whispering, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind…﴾ to the end of the surah.

{201} Since the servant must inevitably be heedless, and Satan, who never ceases to lie in wait, will reach him through that heedlessness, Allah the Exalted mentioned the sign of the God-fearing (muttaqun) as distinct from the misguided (ghawun): when the God-fearing person senses a sin, and a visitation from Satan touches him so that he commits a forbidden act or abandons an obligatory duty, he remembers from which gate he was approached and by which entrance Satan entered upon him. He remembers what Allah has made obligatory for him and the requirements of faith that are upon him. Then he sees clearly, seeks forgiveness from Allah the Exalted, and makes up for what he neglected through sincere repentance and abundant good deeds. Thus his satan is turned back, humiliated and exhausted, having had all that it gained from him ruined.

{202} As for the brothers of the devils and their allies: when they fall into sins, the devils continually extend them in error, sin after sin, and they do not fall short in that. The devils do not fall short of them in misguidance, because they have been greedy for them, having seen them submissive to their control, and they do not hold back from doing evil.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 7, verse 203:

{203} That is: these deniers of yours continue in obstinacy and stubborn opposition, even if the signs indicating guidance and right direction came to them. When you bring them some of the signs indicating your truthfulness, they do not submit. {And when you do not bring them a sign}: from the signs of suggestion that they specify, {they say: "Why do you not invent it?"}; that is: "Why do you not choose the sign, so that it becomes such-and-such a sign or such-and-such a miracle?" As if you were the one who sends down the signs and governs all creatures, and they did not know that you have no say in the matter at all. Or [the meaning is]: "Why do you not invent it from yourself?" {Say: "I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord."}: I am a servant who follows and is governed. Almighty God is the One who sends down the signs and dispatches them according to what His praiseworthiness requires and what His far-reaching wisdom demands. So if you want a sign that does not perish over the succession of times and a proof that does not become void in any moment, then here it is: the Mighty Qur'an and the Wise Reminder. {Insights from your Lord}: by which one gains insight into all divine matters and human purposes. It is both the proof and that which is proven. Whoever reflects upon it and contemplates it knows that it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, falsehood does not come to it from before it or behind it, and by it the proof is established against everyone who has received it. But most people do not believe. Otherwise, whoever believes, for him it is {guidance} from error, and {mercy} from misery. So the believer is guided by the Qur'an, follows it, and is happy in his worldly life and his Hereafter. As for whoever does not believe in it, he is astray and wretched in this world and the Hereafter.

{204} This command is general, applying to everyone who hears the Book of Allah being recited, for he is commanded to listen to it and to be attentive (inṣāt). The difference between listening (istimāʿ) and attentive silence (inṣāt) is that inṣāt is outward, by refraining from speaking or from occupying oneself with what distracts from hearing it, whereas istimāʿ to it means that one lends it one's hearing, presents one's heart, and reflects upon what one hears. Whoever constantly observes these two matters when the Book of Allah is recited will attain much good, abundant knowledge, faith that is continual and renewed, increasing guidance, and insight into his religion. For this reason Allah linked the attainment of mercy to them, which indicates that whoever has the Book recited to him but does not listen to it and remain attentive is deprived of his share of mercy and has missed much good.

Among the most emphasized things the listener of the Qur'an is commanded to do is to listen to it and remain attentive during the audibly recited prayer when his imam recites; for he is commanded to remain attentive, to the extent that most scholars say that his occupation with attentive silence is better than his recitation of al-Fatihah and other passages.

{205} Remembrance of Allah the Exalted occurs in the heart, occurs on the tongue, and occurs with both together. This last is the most perfect of the kinds and states of remembrance. So Allah commanded His servant and Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), primarily, and those after him by extension, to remember their Lord within themselves, that is, sincerely and in solitude. ﴿Humbly﴾, that is, humbly with your tongue, repeating the various forms of remembrance. ﴿And in fear﴾ in your heart, by being fearful of Allah, with a heart trembling before Him, fearing that your deed may not be accepted. A sign of this fear is that one strives and exerts oneself to perfect and correct the deed and to give sincere advice regarding it. ﴿And without loudness in speech﴾, that is, be moderate. Do not raise your voice in your prayer, nor whisper it, but seek a middle way between that. ﴿In the mornings﴾, the beginning of the day, ﴿and the evenings﴾, its end. These two times have a distinction and excellence over others for the remembrance of Allah. ﴿And do not be among the heedless﴾, those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves. They have been deprived of the good of this world and the Hereafter, and they turned away from Him in whose remembrance and worship lies all happiness and success, and they turned toward that in whose occupation with other than Him lies all wretchedness and loss.

This is one of the etiquettes which the servant should observe with due care: frequent remembrance of Allah throughout the hours of the night and day, especially at the two ends of the day, sincerely, humbly, submissively, humbly submitting, with a heart and tongue in agreement regarding it, with courtesy and dignity, turning earnestly to supplication and remembrance, bringing the heart to it, and without heedlessness. For Allah does not respond to a supplication from a heedless, distracted heart.

{206} Then the Exalted mentioned that He has servants who are constantly devoted to His worship and continually in His service, and they are the angels. So know that Allah does not desire that your worship increase His number out of need, nor that He be strengthened by it out of weakness. Rather, He desires the benefit of your own selves, and that you gain from Him many times over what you have done. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, those who are with your Lord﴾, that is, among the angels brought near, the bearers of the Throne and the Karubiyyun (the angels closest to Allah), ﴿do not disdain His worship﴾, but rather submit to it and comply with the commands of their Lord, ﴿and they exalt Him﴾ night and day without ceasing, ﴿and to Him alone﴾, with no partner, ﴿they prostrate﴾. So let the servants follow these noble angels, and let them persevere in the worship of the King, the All-Knowing.

The tafsir (explanation) of Surah al-A'raf is complete.
All praise, thanks and commendation belong to Allah. May Allah send blessings and peace upon Muhammad, his family and his companions.
